text:
Great piece—and remarkable timing calling the fragility at the end of September right before the Q3 FCF shock and the October/November tech drawdown.

That said, I think framing this cycle as "Both Dotcom and 2008" nails the risks in the levered middle layer, but overshoots when applied to upstream semiconductor bottlenecks. Here is how I see what you got right vs. where the thesis goes too far:

Where you nailed it:

- Liquidity & timing: Calling the turn right before hyperscaler Q3 FCF flipped negative (-$30.7B) and CCC junk spreads blew out to 13.14%–13.30% was spot on.
 
- Model-layer commoditization: Open-weight models now account for ~62% of OpenRouter token volume, effective prices fell 57% (closed) and 70% (open) from Jan to Oct, and major enterprise SaaS leaders openly treat LLMs as interchangeable commodities. Pricing power at the pure model layer is clearly compressing.

- Neocloud duration mismatch: Financing multi-year debt against GPUs that obsolete in 1–2 cycles is brutal. CoreWeave’s $846M quarterly net interest and 16%–17% unsecured bond yields—alongside 6.1% US private-credit defaults—prove the high-leverage middlemen are getting squeezed.

Where "Both Dotcom & 2008" overshoots:

- Jevons Paradox vs. 2000 "Dark Fiber": In 2000, fiber sat empty. Today, falling token prices are driving explosive physical compute demand—OpenRouter hit 790T tokens in Oct with agentic keys at 76%, and total compute spend is up ~22x even with 27% lower average token prices. 

- Commoditizing the software layer actually feeds upstream silicon monopolies (TSMC Oct revenue +59.7% YoY, Micron’s 2027 HBM supply largely contracted, and H100 spot rentals still holding $3.06–$3.39/hr).

- SPV ring-fencing & IG credit vs. 2008 contagion: In 2008, interbank and investment-grade credit froze. Today, US IG corporate OAS sits calmly at 0.90% (nowhere near a 250+ bps freeze), hyperscalers hold $2.49T in RPO backlogs, and core Neocloud facilities like CoreWeave's DDTL 4.0 (A3, SOFR+2.25%) are ring-fenced in bankruptcy-remote SPVs backed by investment-grade contracts. Parent equity and unsecured junk debt can get wiped out without triggering a banking collapse.

 - Real enterprise cash flow & bifurcated macro: Unlike 2000's zero-revenue shells, Anthropic is at $81B ARR with +$4.1B in adjusted operating income and a 6x oversubscribed IPO. And while CRE/CMBS delinquencies (8.09% multifamily, 12.33% office) are genuine macro drags, October still added 165k payrolls—pointing to a selective credit shakeout rather than a 2008-style systemic freeze.

Bottom line: Your framework is a great checklist for what to avoid (levered Neocloud equity, low-grade private credit, unmoated model wrappers), but for upstream semiconductor bottlenecks, this looks much more like a mid-cycle valuation reset than Dotcom + 2008.

Hillbilly Hypocrisy: JD Vance and the Dark Future of MAGA Politics

by Nathan J.Robinson

Delivers by Feb 9, 2027

An eye-opening exploration of the man at the center of a movement poised to reshape the fabric of American society.

JD Vance has rapidly risen to power and become the most likely individual to succeed Donald Trump as leader of the MAGA movement. Yet his core political beliefs remain opaque; in only a few years, he has transformed from an outspoken Trump critic into his most enthusiastic enabler. He claims to be a populist everyman, yet he is an ally of both tech oligarchs and dangerous reactionaries. Who is JD Vance, and what does he really believe? Is he an opportunist searching for status, or an ideologue committed to pushing America further into authoritarianism?

Hillbilly Hypocrisy is a study of one of the most mysterious and consequential figures in politics and an urgent examination of the broader MAGA ecosystem from Peter Thiel and Elon Musk to Steve Bannon. Author Nathan J. Robinson argues that the emerging post-Trump right is a vehicle for the self-interested pursuit of power and wealth for a motley group of Christian nationalists and tech overlords with J.D. Vance at its helm. These faux anti-elitists are intent on entrenching inequality and gutting regulations at the expense of the American people.

This deeply-researched and engaging book illuminates the figures vying for control once Trump exits public life. It is vital reading for anyone who wants to understand the forces that want to dictate the trajectory of our country for decades to come.

💎 Advanced Materials

🧱 Structural Materials
- MIT cast a 3-meter optimized beam in sewn fabric molds, using about one-third the concrete and half the steel of a conventional equal-load design in a laboratory demonstration.
- Meta ($META) committed to buy 180,000 tonnes of cement-equivalent Environmental Attribute Certificates from Sublime Systems, supporting a US low-carbon-cement plant. The agreement covers certificates rather than physical cement delivery.

🔬 Nano & Metamaterials
- Zhejiang University and UT Austin researchers constructed a two-dimensional triaxially woven molecular polymer network, extending the architectures available for engineered materials. The Nature paper appeared November 4.
- MIT and Northeastern researchers designed scale-rich network metamaterials that varied stiffness and resisted sudden impacts better than ordered comparators in physical tests. Applications such as protective equipment remain prospective.

💡 Electronic, Photonic & Superconducting Materials
- HKU researchers demonstrated a six-device gallium-oxideide module repeatedly switching 1,000 volts and 1,000 amperes at 1 kHz, achieving megawatt peak power in laboratory tests using junction-side cooling.
- Kyulux plans mass production of precious-metal-free Hyperfluorescence OLED emitting materials as early as 2028. The startup is still seeking commercialization funding.
- E Ink ($8069.TWO) launched a nine-base-color Spectra 6 upgrade, adopted for Aura’s 10-inch Ink e-paper photo frame to improve color transitions and photographic images.
- JNTC ($204270.KQ) completed a Vietnam HDD glass-platter line with annual capacity of 120–170 million units for Seagate ($STX), targeting operations in Q1 2027 and a shipment ramp in Q2.
- Mitsui Chemicals ($4183.T) agreed to acquire JSR at a ¥1.84 trillion enterprise value including assumed debt and obligations, backed by DBJ. Completion is targeted for October 2027–March 2028.
- Mitsui Kinzoku ($5706.T) plans a ¥190 billion ($1.2 billion) Malaysian copper-foil factory, with staged operations beginning April 2031 for high-end electronic materials.
- Doosan ($000150.KS) signed a 550-billion-won memorandum for Changshu copper-clad-laminate expansion, with phased construction and operations targeted for the second half of 2028.
- Toray Advanced Materials Korea completed an MLCC-film capacity expansion from 600 million to 900 million square meters annually, a 50% increase.
- Nan Ya Plastics ($1303.TW) approved NT$11.53 billion for a fifth Changbin fiberglass-cloth plant, targeting 100 million meters annually of thin and ultra-thin cloth for high-end electronics.
- Xianrui signed a letter of intent to supply 6-inch indium-phosphide substrates to Coherent ($COHR) facilities in 2027–2029, with estimated value of at least $601 million.

🔋 Battery & Energy Materials
- Researchers demonstrated a vertically aligned liquid-crystalline-polymer separator that retained 94% of initial lithium-metal-battery capacity after 100 cycles at a 4C charging rate in laboratory tests.
- A UCL-led team designed an electrolyte enabling four-electron iodine reactions in aqueous batteries, avoiding the highly corrosive electrolyte approach used in earlier research.
- USTC collaborators screened interface materials with AI; a synthesized candidate produced a 27.2%-efficient perovskite device, retaining about 95% of initial efficiency after 2,000 hours at 65°C under continuous-light maximum-power-point testing.
- General Motors ($GM) outlined a fourth-generation EV battery plan using lithium-manganese-rich prismatic cells, targeting 33% higher energy density at lithium-iron-phosphate cost. These are development targets.
- Aleees ($5227.TWO) signed a North American partnership memorandum outlining a 25,000-tonne annual Taiwan LFP line for trials and qualification. Investment terms remain unresolved, and a US rollout depends on certification and approvals.
- LS MnM completed an Onsan nickel-sulfate plant with annual capacity equivalent to 24,000 tonnes of nickel metal, designed to process mixed-hydroxide feedstock and recycled battery black mass.

text:
Beau Bayh promised in campaign commercials to "Get rid of corruption" in the state. What does he plan to do to deliver on his promise to Indiana voters who elected him? What does he plan to do with our election system in Indiana? What is his position on fraud, illegal aliens present in Indiana, crime in Indianapolis?

GROK says:

Beau Bayh (Democrat) was elected Indiana Secretary of State in November 2026 and is set to take office on January 1, 2027. He is the son of former Gov./Sen. Evan Bayh, a Harvard-educated attorney and former Marine Corps captain. His central campaign theme was cleaning up alleged corruption and waste in the outgoing Diego Morales (R) administration.
⁠Ballotpedia

Delivering on “Get rid of corruption”

Bayh’s top priority and repeated campaign promise focused on the Secretary of State’s office itself. He cited examples such as a roughly $92,000 luxury SUV, family members hired into high-paying roles, no-bid contracts linked to campaign donors, and questions about travel/spending.⁠
Indystar

His stated plans include:

Launching an independent/forensic audit of the office’s finances, contracts, travel, and hiring on day one (or immediately), with findings made public.
Referring any evidence of illegality to prosecutors/law enforcement.

Involving Republican Knox County Clerk David Shelton (described as a fraud-detection expert) to help oversee the audit for bipartisan credibility.

A personal pledge not to award Secretary of State contracts to his own campaign donors, plus competitively bidding contracts.

Additional ethics steps, such as barring campaign staff from contacting state employees about state business and prohibiting individual stock trading by      himself and top staff.⁠
Mirrorindy

These were framed as restoring trust after what he called insider dealing and waste under the prior Republican officeholder. Critics noted his own large out-of-state donations (including ties linked to his father’s network) and questioned whether the audit would be fully independent.⁠
Wndu

Plans for Indiana’s election system

Bayh’s main election-process proposals center on participation and competition rather than major new restrictions:

Ending  straight-ticket voting (Indiana is one of the few states that still has it). He argues this would force voters to consider individual candidates, increase competition, and raise turnout.

Supporting citizen-led ballot initiatives/referendums so voters can weigh in directly on issues (e.g., redistricting).

Preserving mail-in/absentee and early voting, with possible interest in extending Election Day hours for working families.

Supporting the state’s existing voter ID law and stating that Indiana elections are already “safe and secure,” crediting bipartisan county clerks.⁠
Wthitv

He has expressed skepticism about some federal proposals (such as certain proof-of-citizenship documentation requirements under ideas like the SAVE Act), calling some of them potentially burdensome or unnecessary given existing state systems, and has criticized unnecessary sharing of voter data with Washington without clear need.⁠
Insideindianabusiness

Position on fraud

Bayh has repeatedly said there should be “no illegal votes—period,” “one illegal vote is too many,” and that every instance of fraud should be prosecuted to the full extent of the law. He supports Indiana’s voter ID law as a safeguard. In debates he criticized the prior Republican administration for identifying potential noncitizen voting cases (including reports of noncitizens registered and some ballots cast) but not moving quickly to prosecution, while also calling some of his opponent’s framing of the issue “ridiculous” and saying current systems already prevent noncitizen voting (which is already illegal).
⁠Mirrorindy

Illegal aliens / noncitizens in Indiana

Bayh has not issued broad public positions on immigration enforcement, deportation, or the presence of illegal aliens outside the election context. The Secretary of State’s core duties are elections, business filings, and related administrative matters—not immigration enforcement (which involves federal agencies, the state Attorney General, and local law enforcement).

On the election-specific issue, his position is that noncitizen voting is illegal and should be prosecuted, existing voter ID helps prevent it, and elections are secure. He has pushed back against claims that stronger citizenship-verification steps are urgently needed beyond current law, describing some proposals as fear-mongering that could discourage legitimate participation.⁠
Cms.stateaffairs

Crime in Indianapolis
No specific positions or plans from Bayh on Indianapolis/Marion County crime rates, policing, or related issues appear in his campaign materials or coverage. Those matters fall outside the Secretary of State’s authority (they involve local government, the mayor, police, prosecutors, and the state Attorney General).

In short, Bayh’s concrete commitments center on auditing and reforming the Secretary of State’s office for alleged waste and self-dealing, plus process changes like ending straight-ticket voting and adding citizen initiatives, while affirming support for existing voter ID and prosecuting illegal votes. Broader topics like statewide immigration enforcement or Indianapolis crime were not central to his campaign messaging for this office.

How can Beau Bayh get rid of Straight ticket voting if voters in Indiana prefer it?

GROK says:

Beau Bayh cannot unilaterally eliminate straight-ticket voting.

It is established by Indiana state law, so only the General Assembly can repeal or change it. As Secretary of State (taking office January 1, 2027), Bayh has no authority to rewrite election statutes on his own.⁠
https://t.co/RQXrmb3XTX

He has described ending it as a legislative priority and noted that “there’s at least some Republicans in the Statehouse that agree with me.” He has framed it as a multi-year effort that would require working with the legislature, not something he could impose on day one. Recent attempts illustrate the challenge: Republican-authored bills such as HB 1133 (Rep. Cory Criswell) and HB 1218 (Rep. Edward Clere) to eliminate straight-ticket voting were introduced in 2026 but did not advance, while a bill expanding it (HB 1377) passed and became law. Prior efforts over the past decade have also failed.⁠
Indianacitizen

On whether Indiana voters prefer it

Bayh’s position is that the practice is poor policy regardless of short-term partisan effects. He argues it reduces competition, reinforces tribal “red team / blue team” voting, makes people feel outcomes are predetermined, and lowers incentives to participate or hold individual candidates accountable. He has said he supports ending it even though it could hurt Democrats in places like Marion County (where straight-ticket Democratic ballots far outnumbered Republican ones in 2026).⁠
Indianacapitalchronicle

Available polling does not show clear majority preference for keeping the system:

A October 2025 survey of 604 registered Indiana voters (North Star Opinion Research, for Independent Indiana) found 62% viewed straight-ticket voting as a “bad thing” versus 26% who called it a “good thing.” Even among Republicans, more viewed it negatively (49% bad / 36% good).

One Republican legislator (Criswell) reported that roughly 60% of respondents in his district survey supported eliminating it.

Usage is high where available—over 50% of voters in the largest counties in recent elections, and substantial shares in places like Marion County—but that reflects convenience when the option exists, not necessarily a preference for the policy itself. Indiana is one of only six states that still offer it (alongside Alabama, Kentucky, Michigan, Oklahoma, and South Carolina); most other states have eliminated it over the past few decades.
⁠https://t.co/d1VO8ZcW1Y

In short, Bayh’s path is advocacy and coalition-building in a Republican-controlled legislature, not executive fiat. Whether that succeeds depends on legislative votes, not on his preferences or any single poll.

text:
$UNI flipped short while its established daily regime was still rising strongly. Kong Score: 23, Noise tier.

This is a useful worked example of how Kong Cloud treats a counter-trend event when the surrounding structure has not yet turned with it.

The regime model identified a staircase of six steps across 158 bars, covering 34.14 ATR before the flip. That matters because Kong Cloud does not give every directional change the same structural meaning. In a strong trending regime, a counter-trend event begins with a structural factor of 0.35. The same event after a weak trend receives more credit because the prior direction has less structural persistence.

That 0.35 factor is the first restraint in today's reading. The system has detected a short state, but the broader frame still describes an established rise. The event is therefore evidence of tension inside the regime, not proof that the regime itself has changed.

Pattern evidence becomes especially important on this path. Kong's trending model assigns pattern a weight of 40, the largest component weight, because a recognized reversal formation can supply structural context that a cloud cross alone cannot. Edwards and Magee formalized the distinction between an ordinary interruption and a completed reversal structure. Bulkowski later measured formation behavior statistically. Kong uses that principle as a scoring hierarchy: the flip identifies a state change, while pattern evidence asks whether price structure supports a larger transition.

No reversal pattern was present at the frame's top for this prime. The pattern component therefore contributed 0.0. That absence is analytically meaningful because it leaves the counter-trend flip without the model's highest-weight source of confirmation.

Volume offered limited support. Activity measured 1.12 times the rolling baseline, inside Kong's normal 0.8x to 1.5x band, though its direction was increasing. The volume component contributed 12.0. This is participation, but not the expansion above 1.5x that moves into the confirmed band or above 2.0x that qualifies as strong.

The five-day macro view diverged and contributed 0.6. Regime contributed 5.0, while structural context added 5.25. Together with volume, those inputs produced the final score of 23.

The indicator construction matters here too. Wilder's smoothing family reduces sensitivity to isolated price movement, while confirmation logic is designed to prevent every cross from becoming a new state. Murphy's treatment of confirmation offers the broader principle: evidence becomes more informative when independent dimensions agree. Today's dimensions do not agree. Direction flipped short, the regime remained strongly established in the other direction, macro diverged, and no reversal formation appeared.

The next useful information is structural. Does the short state persist long enough to alter the staircase, or does the existing regime absorb the interruption? Until price structure answers that question, the low score is doing exactly what the methodology intends: recording the flip while preserving uncertainty about its significance.

text:
In case you didn't follow the SEC today:

>🏈Oklahoma beat No. 19 Ole Miss 24-17 and then trolled the Rebels with "Wheels on the Bus" over the stadium speakers (vid in replies)

     - The Sooners also blasted "Airplanes" by B.o.B and put an airplane "no smoking" sign on the scoreboard, per ESPN

     - Venables on the crowd: "They were loud, engaged and pissed. Helped us win the game today."

>🏈Ole Miss got one last shot after recovering an onside kick, but Trinidad Chambliss' final pass into the end zone from the OU 29 was knocked down

     - John Mateer ran for an 8-yard TD and Isaiah Sategna III took a punt back 75 yards for a 14-0 OU lead

>🗣️Pete Golding said his players sat on buses for three hours on Friday before the trip was scrapped: "I told the players this very much felt like COVID-19 to me."

>🗣️Chris Vannini asked why Ole Miss didn't just fly on Saturday afternoon and go straight to the stadium, like K-State did at TCU

>📊Brett McMurphy's "weird stat": Oklahoma has played football since 1895 and has never lost a Sunday SEC home game (they're 1-0 😂)

>🏟️The SEC moved Texas A&M at Oklahoma next Saturday to 3:45 p.m. ET from noon. Venables: "I'll take every minute we can get."

>🗣️Lane Kiffin said he's not taking a "shot," but LSU's high school recruiting wasn't good enough under Brian Kelly: "If they did a better job, we wouldn't be here," per Jon Blau

>📝Mississippi State fired OL coach Phil Loadholt and special teams coordinator Cliff Odom a day after the 41-9 loss to Auburn, its sixth straight loss

     - Lebby said on Nov. 9 he'd wait until after the season on staff changes, per the Clarion Ledger

     - Loadholt made $700,000 this season and Odom $400,000

>📝LSU flipped Marksville (La.) DB Devin Lavalais from Tulane: "I'm staying home. Purple and Gold," he told Rivals

     - That's 17 commits in LSU's 2027 class, per Jon Blau

>🏀No. 7 Texas beat Baylor 75-72 in San Antonio. Isaiah Johnson had 26 and went 4-for-4 from 3

     - Matas Vokietaitis added 14 and 10 boards, plus the late dunk that put Texas ahead for good

>🏀Missouri beat Marquette 69-64 at the United Center in Chicago behind 17 from Jason Crowe Jr. The Tigers scored 39 in the second half

>⚽South Carolina won the SEC soccer tournament, beating Texas 4-1 for its first tournament title since 2017. Kinley Brown scored twice

>🏈SEC pros on Sunday:

     - Dak Prescott (Mississippi State) threw for 343 yards and 5 TDs, but Dallas lost 46-40 to the 49ers

     - George Pickens (Georgia) caught 11 passes for 145 yards and 3 TDs in the same game

     - Drew Lock (Missouri) helped Seattle beat the Raiders 21-13

     - Carson Beck (Georgia) made his NFL debut in Arizona's 34-6 loss to the Rams

>🏈Tennessee WR Mike Matthews is out for the season with a right knee injury, per ESPN and On3. He leads the Vols with 608 receiving yards and 4 TDs

     - Adam Sparks says he's the 10th Vol with a season-ending injury, the most in the SEC

     - QB George MacIntyre isn't expected to miss time with his knee injury, per Pete Nakos

     - The Vols host LSU on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET

>🏀LSU women's guard MiLaysia Fulwiley (17.8 ppg) was arrested on Saturday night, accused of hitting a police vehicle while fleeing a traffic stop, per ESPN

     - Charges include aggravated battery and flight from an officer. She posted that she "would NEVER in my life hit a police!"

     - LSU hosts Troy on Monday night, and her status was unclear

Was Oklahoma's bus trolling S tier or too much?

Let me know what I missed 👇

Follow @wakeupSEC for this every night. #SEC

text:
A Lannister Pays His Debts, but a CFO Asks for Receipts

In Game of Thrones, nobody wins a war without the Iron Bank. Kings come and go but it's the bank who decides who has an army.

For three years the Iron Bank of AI wore a leather jacket. On Thursday Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia.

The why is not my department.

The what-now is: the bank now belongs to its CFO.

Here's the deal - . A year ago Nvidia held $7 billion of stock in other companies. Today, $99 billion. It has guaranteed $108 billion of other people's leases and promised $36 billion to buy capacity its own customers can't sell. It sold you the shovel, financed the shovel, and co-signed the mortgage on the mine. It can afford all of it; it makes $150 billion a year in cash. Debt capacity was never the question. Risk appetite is.

I wrote in September that history rhymes. In 2000 Nortel bought its growth with its stock. Nvidia bought its growth with its signature. Nortel's currency was inflated. Nvidia's is real, which is better, and personal, which is worse. In 1907 J.P. Morgan stopped a panic by locking the bankers in his library. When he died it took an act of Congress to replace him. One man's judgment is a fine financial system right up to the funeral.

Three things follow.

1. The neoclouds lose their sponsor.

Colette Kress is interim, and she defended these deals in public. She is also, per the Journal, the one who cut the OpenAI guarantee in half before signing it, and who kept asking how the returns were calculated, a question that has ended many a party. Old promises get kept. New ones get a committee. A neocloud is a business made entirely of new ones. Nvidia borrows at under 6%. CoreWeave's bonds yield nearly 15%. The guarantee turned the second number into the first. Without it, interest is the only thing still compounding. The hare just found out who was buying the carrots.

2. Open weights just got heavy.

Nvidia pledged $26 billion to open models because free models sell chips, and Jensen was Washington's loudest voice against export controls. Patron and lobbyist, gone in one afternoon. Disclosure: Menlo backs a frontier  lab, so I'm describing a competitor's misfortune. Discount accordingly. But our own data says open models are 19% of enterprise tokens and 4% of the spend. That's a movement that needs a benefactor. And the Senate majority leader now calls new chip restrictions a "high probability." The night is dark and full of covenants.

3. The bar tab needs a new card.

The guarantees were a bridge across the diffusion gap: Nvidia lending against 2030 to an economy still living in 1919. Pull the bridge and watch. The boomerang comes home: Nvidia has ordered $279 billion of parts for customers who just lost their financing. Cisco tried that in 2001 and wrote off the warehouse. The co-signer picks the chip: the Ohio guarantee came with a clause, Nvidia hardware only, and the hyperscalers can read. He who signs the lease picks the silicon. And none of it shows yet. The old deals run six years. The hole opens in 2028 and 2029, exactly when the tab comes due.

Two weeks ago the voters took away the permits. This week the board took away the co-signer. I asked a month ago whose card was open. It was Jensen's. He was the man at the end of the bar saying "put it on mine," and the room mistook his generosity for its own credit.

The music's still playing. But the man with the open tab has left, and his cfo would like to see some receipts.

THE RECORD: Carney in Manila: Europe's security will be set "by free Europe and NATO, not by Russia." 🐿️ Lovely. So who set Canada's war bill and digital future? Not one ballot we could find. h/t @D21158Dragon @DietHeartNews @brivael
🔹 THE RECEIPTS • Canadian Press and CBC, Nov 14 2026, Manila news conference. Carney: "There's no way that Canada as a NATO member is going to walk away from any other NATO member — ever." Then: "The security architecture for free Europe will be determined by free Europe and NATO, not by Russia and a redux of the Minsk agreement." He cited 2,500 Canadian troops leading the NATO brigade in Latvia. • DND: about 2,000 CAF members are in Latvia under Op REASSURANCE. Carney announced at the Ankara NATO summit in July 2026 that the mission is extended to 2031. Budget 2026: $7.6B over five years, enough for up to 2,600 persistently deployed troops. DND planned about $950M in incremental costs for 2026-27 alone. • DND, Feb 24 and Mar 2026: 383 Roshel Senators and 66 GD LAV 6s for Ukraine. Roshel's CEO told a Senate committee that Canada has bought more than 500 for Ukraine and "zero" for our own Army, "including those in Latvia." • Lobbying registry: Roshel has filed dozens of communication reports through consultants in the past year, meeting with DND, ISED and MPs. All legal and registered. • Global Affairs Canada: more than $25.5B committed to Ukraine since Russia's 2022 invasion. Carney pledged 5% of GDP to NATO in The Hague. The PBO says the 3.5% core share alone means $163.6B a year by 2035-36. We found no standalone Commons vote on either. • @brivael's thread, checked: Klaus Schwab at the Harvard Kennedy School in 2017 said of Young Global Leaders, "we penetrate the cabinets," and that "more than half" of Trudeau's cabinet were YGLs. The UN and the WEF signed a partnership on June 13 2019 to accelerate Agenda 2030. WEF annual reports list Carney (until Jan 2025) and Freeland (2023-24) as WEF trustees. • EU: the digital euro bill was tabled in June 2023. The Parliament's economic affairs committee passed it 43-14 on June 23 2026, and its chair Aurore Lalucq called it "a historic day for Europe." Target: 2029. Also coming: a €10,000 EU-wide cash cap from July 2027, a digital ID wallet in every member state by end of 2026, and a carbon price on heating and fuel (ETS2) delayed to 2028. • NOT FOUND: any primary record of Carney saying "Russia has no rights…" or of him laughing, or any vote by Canadians on any of the above. The 2016 WEF line "you'll own nothing" came from Danish MP Ida Auken's essay, which the WEF calls a scenario. The Bank of Canada shelved a retail digital dollar in Sept 2023.
OPINION Davos drafts the scenario. Brussels turns it into regulation. A NATO summit sets the budget. Then a PM tells reporters in Manila that Europe gets to decide its own future. We agree, and we'd like the same deal. @brivael calls it the "World Communist Forum." We'll just call it the club where your vote isn't on the guest list. The Senators roll out of Brampton for Kyiv while our own troops in Latvia get none. The tab hits $163 billion a year. And the only people never consulted are the ones paying for the gas, the tanks and the app.
HOW TO STOP THEM, LAWFULLY
Alberta first: ask your MLA and Alberta's Finance Minister to put Alberta's share of the 5% NATO cost on the record in writing.
Write your MP and ask for a standalone Commons vote on the 5% pledge and on the Op REASSURANCE extension to 2031.
File an Access to Information request with DND for the contract values of the 383 Senators and the Latvia mission's full cost.
Search the federal lobbying registry yourself for Roshel and General Dynamics, and keep a list of who they met.
Ask your MP to put in writing that Canada will never launch a digital dollar or national digital ID without an Act of Parliament.
If Europe gets to decide Europe's security, when do Canadians get to vote on Canada's? 👇

WINNIE BYANYIMA DISPUTES CLAIMS OF KIZZA BESIGYE’S IMPROVED HEALTH AND WARNS GOVERNMENT AGAINST PLAYING POLITICAL FOOTBALL WITH HIS LIFE.

By Keefa Nuwahereza.
On Sunday, 15 November 2026, Winnie Byanyima, the wife of detained Ugandan opposition leader Dr Kizza Besigye, held a press conference at the family’s home in Kasangati, Wakiso District. In a direct challenge to statements from Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Norbert Mao, she disputed claims that Besigye’s health had improved following his transfer to a clinic. Byanyima argued that the facility lacks the capacity to deliver the specialised treatment her husband requires, and that ongoing restrictions on access for his personal doctor create serious risks in the event of an emergency.

Wearing one of Besigye’s shirts as a gesture of solidarity, Byanyima described a man whose physical condition has deteriorated sharply since his detention began roughly two years earlier. She stated that the four-time presidential candidate, a retired army colonel and former physician who once served as President Yoweri Museveni’s personal doctor, can no longer walk short distances without assistance. He relies on crutches and needs someone beside him. His right hand, she said, has become largely lifeless and shakes, while his left hand, which he does not normally use, is unstable and cannot reliably hold a pen. “This is a man who cannot write,” she told journalists. “Today he is a man who cannot walk even from here to the end of this plot.”

These descriptions follow a series of medical crises during Besigye’s detention. In late July 2026, he collapsed and lost consciousness in the dock during a High Court hearing in his treason trial, after objecting to the appointment of state-funded lawyers. He was taken to Mulago National Referral Hospital’s intensive care unit. Byanyima reported at the time that he arrived unconscious and unresponsive, and that he refused treatment from government doctors in favour of his personal physician. Later transfers, including to the Joint Clinical Research Centre, occurred amid continued family concerns that available care was inadequate. Byanyima has previously appealed for permission to take him to Geneva for specialised treatment, where family support would be available, with a commitment that he would return to face charges once recovered.

Byanyima’s remarks on 15 November specifically countered Mao’s assertions about improvement after the clinic transfer. She maintained that those offering public assurances either lacked accurate information or were advancing a political agenda. “There is no assurance anyone can give, unless they have a political agenda, that this man is okay. He is not okay,” she said. She added that the family remained uncertain about developments inside his body because he was not under the care of appropriate specialists. Restrictions limiting his personal doctor’s involvement, she argued, left him vulnerable should another emergency arise.

In her strongest statement, Byanyima warned the government against what she called “playing political football with the life of a human being.” She declared that the family would not accept being informed of his death in custody and then asked to collect his body. “And they must not give me a message ‘Kizza Besigye is dead, come and take his body.’ No, no, no. That won’t be acceptable.” She questioned repeated refusals of bail, asking whether authorities were waiting for him to die, and reiterated calls for his release on bail so that he could receive the medical attention she believes he urgently needs.

Byanyima also raised separate concerns about former Kampala Lord Mayor Erias Lukwago, who is held at the same facility. She said Lukwago had suffered two medical emergencies within a single week without timely attention, and that authorities had barred the two men from communicating with each other. These points underscored broader questions about medical care for opposition figures in detention.

Besigye’s case has a clear political dimension. He was arrested in Nairobi, Kenya, on 16 November 2024 while attending a book launch, then brought to Uganda and charged with treason and related offences alongside aides including Hajji Obed Lutale. After a Supreme Court ruling limited military trials of civilians, the case moved to civilian courts. The prosecution alleges a plot to overthrow the government by force of arms; the accusations have not been proven. Besigye, a long-standing critic of Museveni’s government, has faced multiple previous arrests and trials. His current detention has drawn national and international attention, particularly after the court collapse and subsequent hospitalisations.

Political dialogue efforts have added another layer. President Museveni’s brother, Gen Salim Saleh, has been involved in backchannel discussions. Saleh has stated that he found Besigye in a life-threatening condition in prison and arranged a transfer for treatment. He has also indicated that release could occur within three to six months. Byanyima, however, ruled out any national dialogue between the government and the opposition under the present climate, insisting that her husband’s health and freedom should not be subjects of political negotiation. Minister Mao has previously framed three parallel tracks—court proceedings, medical care, and political engagement—while acknowledging that specialised treatment unavailable in Uganda may be required and that bail would be needed for travel abroad. Doctors have advised that such treatment could accelerate recovery, and the trial has been halted at times because Besigye could not fully participate in his defence.

Prisons authorities have at times issued more optimistic assessments, stating that both Besigye and Lukwago were improving and that care was being coordinated with personal doctors. Family accounts and Byanyima’s public statements have consistently presented a different picture of weakness, restricted mobility, and limited access to trusted specialists. These discrepancies have fuelled ongoing debate about whether detention conditions and medical arrangements meet required standards.

The Kasangati press conference crystallises a prolonged standoff. For Byanyima, the priority remains securing bail so that Besigye can obtain specialised care outside the constraints of detention facilities. For the government, the case involves concurrent judicial, medical, and political considerations, with officials maintaining that appropriate care is being provided while legal processes continue. As of mid-November 2026, Besigye remains detained, his health a subject of public dispute, and his wife’s warning against treating his life as a political bargaining chip has placed the human stakes of the prolonged case in sharp relief. The coming weeks will test whether medical assessments, court decisions, or political calculations ultimately determine the conditions under which he receives further treatment.

text:
Ukraine says restrictions affecting its use of SpaceX’s Starshield satellite communications system remain widespread, hampering the military’s ability to intercept Russian jet-powered attack drones near the front line and giving Moscow additional opportunities to strike Ukrainian targets.

Denys Sienik, Ukraine’s top diplomat in Washington, told RFE/RL on November 14 that Ukrainian forces continue to experience disruptions despite repeated tests in multiple directions.

“As of today, I can confirm that the restrictions are effective. These are not isolated cases; they are widespread,” Sienik said.

“Because of this, we can intercept Russian jet-powered UAVs only after they enter the territory controlled by Ukraine. Hence, we can’t shoot them down immediately near the front line. This gives Russians more leverage which they haven’t had so far.”

“For example, our Bars units operate using Starshield. They shoot down jet-powered Shaheds. Now we can’t shoot them down there, near the front line,” he said. Instead, Ukrainian forces must wait until the drones reach other defensive lines.

Sienik said the disruptions had persisted for five days, with Ukrainian officials conducting daily tests and obtaining the same results.

SpaceX Denies Restrictions

The Ukrainian Defense Ministry has raised the issue directly with SpaceX, but the company has rejected allegations that it introduced restrictions.

According to Ukrainian officials who spoke to RFE/RL on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to comment publicly, SpaceX told the ministry: “We are not imposing any restrictions.”

The company referred to technical issues but did not respond to a follow-up question about the situation in temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories, the Ukrainian officials said.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has also challenged SpaceX's explanation, saying Kyiv does not believe the disruptions are simply technical problems.

Zelenskyy said Starshield terminals operating in temporarily Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories had been subject to speed restrictions of approximately 161 kilometers per hour for five days.

He said the restrictions had political implications, arguing that limiting the service in occupied territories risked treating those areas differently from the rest of Ukraine.

“If you impose restrictions there, you are already partially recognizing the temporarily occupied territories as not ours,” Zelenskyy said in remarks released by his office on November 14.

He said he had instructed senior military and foreign ministry officials to pursue the issue with SpaceX and seek the restoration of unrestricted service.

The latest dispute follows a similar episode in October, when Ukrainian officials reported that SpaceX had limited the speed of Starlink and Starshield terminals to approximately 160 kph. Service was reportedly restored on October 24.

SpaceX founder Elon Musk has maintained that Starshield is controlled by the US government, with the military determining restrictions on speed and use and the final authority resting with President Donald Trump. Trump has denied involvement in the restrictions.

Democrats Seek Answers

The disruptions have also drawn growing concern in Washington, where lawmakers from both parties have questioned the extent of private control over communications systems used in Ukraine's defense.

Democratic Senators Jeanne Shaheen and Chris Coons, both members of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, have formally asked Musk to preserve all records related to restrictions on Ukraine's use of Starlink and Starshield.

In a letter made public on November 13, the senators requested documents and communications dating back to September 1, including exchanges involving Musk, SpaceX executives, Ukrainian officials, the White House, and the Pentagon.

They also asked Musk to confirm by November 30 that appropriate safeguards were in place.

Democratic lawmakers in the House also condemned reports of renewed limitations.

Gregory Meeks, the ranking Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Adam Smith, the ranking Democrat on the House Armed Services Committee, said any restrictions on Ukraine's use of Starshield in occupied territories and along the line of contact would be unacceptable if confirmed.

They argued that previous limitations had contributed to Ukrainian civilian casualties, including the deaths of children, and strengthened Russia's position.

The lawmakers pledged to continue pressing for answers and accountability.

Experts Warn Of Dependence

The dispute has renewed questions about Ukraine's dependence on a single private company for critical military communications.

Retired US Army Lieutenant Colonel Amos Fox, a fellow at Arizona State University's Future Security Initiative, told RFE/RL that the situation illustrates the risks of relying on a single provider for essential military capabilities.

“A challenger to Musk’s dominance of this space would help insulate states like Ukraine from the political games of people like Musk,” Fox said.

He also pointed to the influence that individuals outside government can exercise over national security decisions when states depend heavily on their companies and resources.

Paul Poast of the University of Chicago questioned whether the disruptions could be explained by technical problems alone.

While acknowledging that technology outages can occur, Poast told RFE/RL that he doubted the Starshield disruption was simply a glitch.

He noted Musk's previous comments that an earlier slowdown resulted from SpaceX's interpretation of its terms of service and questioned whether the latest disruptions could be connected to diplomatic efforts involving Ukraine and Russia.

Poast raised the possibility that the disruptions could have served as an indirect means of increasing pressure on Kyiv during negotiations, although he offered no evidence establishing such a connection.

Dispute Amid Talks

The Starshield dispute comes as the Trump administration seeks to advance negotiations to end Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine, with questions over territorial concessions and European security remaining contentious.

US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner -- Trump's son-in-law -- said they remained in contact with Moscow, Kyiv, and European partners following trilateral discussions.

In a social media statement on November 14, Kushner said the next phase of negotiations would focus on facilitating direct engagement between Russia and European governments and preparing another round of trilateral talks.

He said several new ideas were being explored and stressed that any eventual agreement must include credible security guarantees for Ukraine.

“President Trump will only support arrangements that strengthen Ukraine’s and Europe’s security and make future conflict less likely,” Kushner wrote.

His comments followed criticism from Republican Senator Tom Cotton, who rejected reported Russian demands that NATO withdraw forces from Eastern Europe.

“NATO nations withdrawing from their own borders is a preposterous demand by Russia,” Cotton said, adding that Moscow would stop fighting only when it understood it could not win.

European leaders have also warned against pressuring Kyiv into territorial concessions.

French President Emmanuel Macron said on November 14 that countries seeking to limit assistance to Ukraine were effectively trying to impose an unjust peace, warning that such an approach could lead to another war.

To the  host and to others on the chat. Good evening it’s a pleasure.

I actually see where you are coming from when looking strictly at the numbers, and sometimes a literal, data driven view is both useful and necessary. Having attended Howard in the late eighties and early nineties before going on to Columbia for graduate school, however, I look at the phrase "The Black Harvard" through a slightly different lens. 

Howard is a good school, and when you hear that nickname, it is easy to view it as a form of misinformation. Think of it like McDonald's. Does the burger ever look exactly like the glossy picture on the menu screen? No, it does not. Yet it is still good, and every now and then you might find a particular location that makes it just like the picture, though nobody is driving cross country just to find that one restaurant. 

Calling it "The Black Harvard" is not false advertising; it is rooted in nostalgia, legacy, and a history that Black Americans built and were a part of. When I was applying to college, I scored a 1520 on my SATs and was accepted into Harvard, and no DEI, buddy the lol , I already had English and two other languages fluently under my belt by then. Although I could only read and write confidently in two of them at that point .

Honestly, the whole Ivy League branding did not attract me like that for my undergraduate years, and I only applied because my guidance counselor pushed me to do it. Do not get me wrong, if you want to go into a certain career, sure, that branding can be helpful, though it is also a question of what is selling and who is buying. 

That gets to a broader misconception surrounding the whole DEI debate, where people often assume every Black student is desperate to get into Harvard and that institutions have to lower their standards just to let them
in. I look at history differently, and I recognize how convenient that narrative can be. 

Even during the era of segregation, most Black Americans were not clamoring simply to sit next to white people; they wanted fairness, equal resources, and respect. That was true for my parents, who came from that era, and it remains true today. Growing up in a wealthy Long Island community as the child of humble, working class parents, with a father who was a sanitation worker and a mother who worked in a hospital laundry, I went to high school alongside kids whose parents were bank presidents, doctors, and lawyers. Wall Street types. A wonderful legacy to inherit. 

My family's legacy  was and  continues to be serving America. Having relatives who fought in all of America's wars, from the American Revolution through the Civil War, both  World Wars  and Korea to Vietnam, carries even more legacy than a Harvard degree. My father spent two years as a LRRP in Vietnam, and to me that was more impressive than any corporate title. The literature he gave me to read in high school included The Autobiography of Malcolm X, Bloods by Wallace Terry, and People's War, People's Army by General Giáp. I realize that in that  capacity as a LRRP he probably saved more lives than he took. And he did take lives, 
ya dig. 

The life lessons I learned from him and others like him were so nuanced and profound that I think even a Distinguished Fellow from an Ivy League institution would find them hard to discern.  Go to whatever school you want because you are going to get the education. Your moral character and your honor, however, are things you should already have by the time you get there. 

That is why so many young people get flipped by their professors; they arrive like an empty cup waiting to be filled, when that cup should have been filled at home long before they ever stepped onto campus. Mine was filled to the brim, and that is why I have always been able to walk the Earth with confidence. 

Do not get me wrong, there is plenty to learn at school, but your principles, integrity and your judgment should already be in hand so you can filter and discern information at a college that goes contrary to your core.

Because I grew up around these examples of courage and sacrifice, I never looked at bright lights or prestigious labels and assumed they were automatically better, even though my father certainly wanted me to get my education. That perspective gave me the nuance and courage  to choose my own path.

 I have always had friends across every background and religion, and I never change my voice or my inflection depending on who is in the room. I am who I am, proud of the distinct identity and history wrapped up inside me.

 I did not choose Howard because I needed a crutch or a safe space; I chose Howard because of my family's Southern roots and pride. For my aunts and my family, Howard carried a level of prestige and cultural weight that Harvard simply could not match. When people call Howard "The Black Harvard," it is somewhat tongue in cheek, rooted in history, tradition, and affection rather than a literal comparison of admissions statistics or endowments. 

Even in the days of Alain Locke, the first African American Rhodes Scholar, a Harvard graduate himself, and a legendary professor at Howard, nobody pretended Howard's resources matched Harvard's. During an era when Black Americans were shut out of the nation's elite institutions, Howard was the pinnacle for Black excellence, and today that nickname endures out of legacy and cultural reverence. 

That core legacy is resilient, too. I remember years ago when there was a big uproar over increasing numbers of white students enrolling in Howard's medical school, and my reaction was simply to let them in. We already had white students on campus, and the core identity of the institution remained intact. 

It is similar to how some white Americans today worry about demographic shifts from ninety percent to sixty percent, when the country's foundational character is still there. Looking only at incoming test scores also leaves out what actually happens once students arrive on campus. First, an ACT score of 25, which is roughly a 1200 SAT, is well above the national average. Second, there is a sizable group of students at Howard who could easily have attended Ivy League universities yet actively chose Howard out of genuine preference rather than necessity. 

With all the current rhetoric treating HBCUs and their students as inferior, people miss the reality that there are groups of students at Black colleges who are every bit as brilliant as, and sometimes sharper than, those at Harvard. At the same time, Howard has always maintained a dual mission. 

I went to school with guys from under resourced neighborhoods who did not score well on their SATs. Howard gave them a chance, and those guys worked relentlessly during their first two years. By the time they were juniors, they were completely ready to compete with anyone in the country. That early support did not lower the bar; it lifted people up to meet it. 

Beyond the academics, there is the sheer joy of the experience itself. When I think about the fun we had, from Homecoming to the camaraderie and just everything else, it brings a smile to my face thinking back on those good old days, even though Washington, D.C., and U Street back then were very rough around the edges. 

That spirit ties directly into the broader conversations happening today around Heritage Americans and “Foundational” Black Americans. For multi generational Black Americans, Howard is more than a university; it is a direct tie to family history and an institution their antecedents help build. 

 Meanwhile, for someone from a recent immigrant background or a white student who chooses to enroll, it offers a completely different kind of draw, a chance to immerse themselves in a vibrant, historic American cultural hub. Their were white students who went there and loved it, and sometimes they ended up having the best dance moves in the place. 😊

Without turning this into a separate debate, I have both white and Black ancestors who fought in the American Revolution, and that shared history is the very construct of the Black American phenotype. For me, going to Howard was never just about getting a degree to become a chemist or checking a career box; it was part of that deeper American identity and sense of duty that weaves everything together. 

I know you probably see it as misrepresentation of fact . In a 
very literal sense, it might be.
There is also the assumption by others that everyone automatically wants or should want to go to Harvard.  It is like assuming everyone should chase the exact same definition of success. Im trained as a historian and taught for several years before moving into an entirely different field in business, and I am genuinely happy with what I am doing and what I have built. 

I have friends who were making tremendous wealth for themselves in the financial markets by their thirties. I could have always chased more money, money was their god and it was never mine. I have made a great living and invested well for myself because I chose what actually suited me. Just because one person values a certain credential or paycheck does not mean everyone else shares that goal. Sure, on paper, Harvard carries more institutional clout and opens certain corporate doors faster, much like people can debate which genre of music is superior even though good music is simply good music. 

But if you are worthy and confident, doors will open for you wherever you go. Sometimes you choose a place simply because it suits who you are, what you value, and where you come from, and that path worked out just fine for me.

Thanks  to the host for posting his thoughts.  It was honest and heartfelt. When information is presented  with civil discourse and rancor subdued, citizens of the world can realize  that great  work can be achieved together. 

Thank you for your time. Tallyho

text:
Abiodun Inaugurates 50,400 APC Canvassers Ahead of 2027 Elections

Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has inaugurated 50,400 grassroots political canvassers of the All Progressives Congress (APC), known as Renewed Hope Apostles, to mobilise support for the party ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The canvassers are expected to embark on coordinated door-to-door campaigns across the state’s 236 wards to promote the achievements of APC-led governments at the federal, state and local government levels.

Abiodun announced the initiative during a series of strategic meetings with APC leaders and stakeholders across Ogun State’s 20 local government areas.

The governor explained that the initiative was designed to strengthen the party’s grassroots presence, improve public understanding of government policies and address misinformation.

He disclosed that 15,000 canvassers had been mobilised in Ogun East, while the total number across the state stood at 50,400.

According to him, the canvassers were carefully selected and organised around polling units to ensure effective engagement with residents at the grassroots. He added that their recruitment and verification process took approximately three months.

Abiodun said the Renewed Hope Apostles would be equipped with information about the achievements of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration and his government’s performance in Ogun State to enable them to communicate the impact of government policies to residents.

Highlighting federal projects benefiting the state, the governor mentioned the reconstruction of the Sagamu-Ijebu-Ode-Ore Road, the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the Gateway Deep Sea Port, the revival of the Ogun LNG project and the establishment of a major Customs facility.

He said the projects were strengthening Ogun State’s economic prospects, attracting investments, creating employment opportunities and supporting industrial development.

The governor also highlighted his administration’s achievements, including the construction of over 1,700 kilometres of roads, rehabilitation and construction of more than 1,600 schools, and provision of over 7,000 housing units.

He further disclosed that 160 primary healthcare centres had been upgraded, while more than 20,000 farmers had benefited from agricultural inputs. He added that over 60,000 women had received support through the Oko Owo Dapo initiative.

On economic empowerment, Abiodun said cooperative societies and artisans had received more than N1 billion in financial support, while over 7,000 teachers had been recruited to strengthen public education.

The governor charged the newly inaugurated canvassers to carry out their responsibilities with commitment and discipline, urging them to engage voters, address their concerns and mobilise support for the APC.

He also called on party leaders and members to put aside personal differences and work together towards electoral success in 2027.

“A divided party cannot win an election. We must work together as a team, strengthen our relationships and ensure that every member understands the importance of this assignment,” Abiodun said.

The governor noted that the stakeholder meetings were also aimed at strengthening internal party unity, reviewing mobilisation strategies and establishing a common direction ahead of the 2027 general elections.

text:
For 31 years, the leaders of China, the United States, and Russia have shared photographs.

On November 19, they will finally share a negotiating table of their own.

And it will happen in China.

Following announcements by the United States and Russia over the weekend, China's Foreign Ministry announced at 9 am Beijing time on November 16 that Chinese President Xi Jinping would hold a trilateral summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President @realDonaldTrump in south China's city of Shenzhen (深圳) on November 19.

I spent some time going through the historical records of meetings between the leaders of these three countries.

And one thing stood out to me:
This appears to be the first dedicated trilateral summit between the heads of state of China, the United States, and Russia in history.

And the historical journey leading to this moment is fascinating.

The earliest event attended simultaneously by the presidents of China, the United States, and Russia appears to date back to May, 1995.

Russia held commemorations in Moscow marking the 50th anniversary of victory in WWII. Chinese President Jiang Zemin (江泽民), US President Bill Clinton, and Russian President Boris Yeltsin attended the military parade in Red Square.

In October of the same year, the three leaders gathered again in New York to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the founding of the United Nations (top right).

Since then, with the development of international multilateral diplomatic mechanisms, the leaders of China, the United States, and Russia have had increasingly frequent opportunities to appear together on the world stage.

In 1998, Russia officially joined APEC. However, then-President Yeltsin did not personally attend Russia's first two APEC Economic Leaders' Meetings, instead sending his premiers to represent the country.

On November 15-16, 2000 (exactly 26 years ago!), Chinese President Jiang Zemin, US President @BillClinton, and Russian President Vladimir Putin all attended the eighth APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held in Brunei (bottom left). 

In October of the following year, the ninth meeting was held in Shanghai (上海), bringing together Jiang, George W. Bush, and Putin (bottom right). I was still in middle school at the time, and I remember watching Jiang deliver a speech in English on live television.

In 2014, China hosted the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting for the second time, with Xi, @BarackObama, and Vladimir Putin in attendance (top left).

The upcoming APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for November 18-19 in Shenzhen, will mark the third time China has hosted the event.

Since the establishment of the G20 leaders' summit mechanism in 2008, the leaders of China, the United States, and Russia have had even more opportunities to cross paths on the international stage.

Yet one particularly intriguing fact stands out:

Over the past three decades, the leaders of China, the United States, and Russia have appeared together in numerous group photographs, but they have never actually sat down at a negotiating table specifically set for a trilateral meeting.

And the September 2000 summit of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council in New York was a five-party meeting, rather than a dedicated trilateral meeting between China, the United States, and Russia.

On November 19, that changes.

Why does this matter?

Here is how I see it:
Diplomacy: bring adversaries together.
Ideas: challenge the logic of inevitable confrontation.
Strategy: maintain relations without choosing sides.
Institutions: turn a historic meeting into lasting dialogue.

The summit's first significance is what it reveals about China's diplomatic convening power. Bringing friends together is easy. Bringing adversaries to the same table is an entirely different matter.

The influence of a great power should be measured not only by whom it can deter, but also by whom it can bring together.

Second, the summit offers an opportunity to challenge some of the most deeply entrenched and flawed assumptions in international relations.

China has long advocated a balanced approach to justice and interests (正确义利观), a vision that fundamentally challenges traditional thinking in IR. In my view, conventional notions such as the primacy of national interests, the security dilemma, and the clash of civilizations are increasingly ill-suited to today's international landscape and serve only to generate unnecessary suspicion, hostility and conflict. This is not a new argument for me.

During my time studying in the Department of Government at Cornell, I repeatedly questioned some of the fundamental assumptions underlying mainstream international relations theory. Yet I often encountered considerable resistance from a few professors and their overzealous TAs who seemed more committed to defending established intellectual paradigms than to examining their limitations.

And I have always wondered:
What happens when a theory designed to explain conflict becomes a prescription for producing it?

One of the great tragedies of American foreign policy, in my view, is that some of its intellectual architects have become so invested in theories of competition and confrontation that they struggle to imagine a world organized around cooperation and mutual benefit.

This summit will provide an important opportunity and a global platform for China to promote its vision of a new type of international relations. Whether China can encourage the world's major powers to move beyond some of their differences and seek common ground will be one of the most important aspects of this meeting to watch.

New ideas about IR are not ultimately judged by how persuasive they sound in academic journals, but by whether they can help make the world a more peaceful place.

Third, China does not need to undermine its relationship with one major power to demonstrate the strength of its relationship with another. 

Does a stronger China-Russia relationship necessarily mean a weaker China-US relationship?

Does improving relations with Washington require Beijing to distance itself from Moscow?

Why should China have to choose?

Washington and Moscow may both hope that China will play a role in addressing certain issues, but whether Beijing will accept the agenda they seek to set remains to be seen.

Fourth, perhaps the most consequential question is what happens after November 19.

Will Shenzhen be remembered as a one-off diplomatic event, or as the beginning of a new mechanism preventing bloc confrontation in international politics?

If the three countries can build on this meeting to establish more stable channels of communication, or even gradually institutionalize regular trilateral summits, its historical significance could extend far beyond that of a single APEC summit.

Some have drawn comparisons between this meeting and the Cairo, Tehran, Yalta, and Potsdam conferences. I do not share that view. The differences in national interests, strategic disagreements, and levels of mutual trust among the three countries mean that establishing such a mechanism will be anything but easy.

Moreover, no mechanism for dialogue among major powers should imply that a handful of powerful countries have the right to determine the fate of others. Its true value should lie in reducing the risk of confrontation, not in dividing the world into spheres of influence.

The world is not short of great-power competition. What it lacks are mechanisms to prevent that competition from spiraling out of control. 

November 19 will give us another historic photograph.

What happens afterward will determine its place in history.

Quiet Diplomacy with the US: The Geopolitical Cost of Strategic Silence

Introduction

🌟 The editorial argues that India's excessive diplomatic silence towards American unilateralism may undermine its credibility as a champion of a rules-based international order. It advocates principled, calibrated diplomacy rather than unconditional accommodation of powerful nations.

Main Body

🌟 Quiet Diplomacy versus Public Silence: India's preference for behind-the-scenes negotiations may offer short-term advantages but risks weakening its international moral authority.

🌟 Historical Diplomatic Legacy: India condemned colonial interventions in Indonesia and Indochina in 1946 and the US invasion of Iraq in 2003, demonstrating its commitment to international norms.

🌟 Erosion of Normative Consistency: The article highlights India's restrained responses to several controversial international developments, including the Ukraine conflict, Hong Kong, Iran and other instances of alleged unilateral action.

🌟 Strategic Accommodation: Excessive caution towards Washington may protect immediate bilateral interests but weaken India's ability to influence global diplomatic narratives.

🌟 China's Geopolitical Opportunity: India's silence can create diplomatic space for Beijing to emerge as an alternative partner for countries facing American pressure.

🌟 International Norms and Institutions: Consistent criticism of violations helps strengthen international law, institutional accountability and multilateral cooperation.

🌟 India's Global Leverage: Its economic scale, military capabilities and strategic position give India considerable potential to influence international opinion.

Challenges

🌟 Managing strategic dependence on the US.

🌟 Balancing national interests with normative commitments.

🌟 Preventing diplomatic criticism from damaging bilateral cooperation.

🌟 Countering geopolitical polarisation and great-power pressure.

Constructive Criticism

🌟 Silence may be interpreted as tacit acceptance of unilateralism.

🌟 Selective application of principles weakens diplomatic credibility.

🌟 Excessive accommodation creates normative inconsistency.

🌟 Moral leadership requires consistent positions, not occasional declarations.

Way Forward

🌟 Adopt principled and calibrated public diplomacy.

🌟 Strengthen strategic autonomy and multi-alignment.

🌟 Uphold international law consistently across geopolitical conflicts.

🌟 Use multilateral platforms to build diplomatic coalitions.

🌟 Combine discreet negotiations with transparent articulation of national positions.

Highlighted Keywords

Strategic Autonomy | Normative Consistency | Rules-Based Order | Quiet Diplomacy | Normative Power | Multilateralism | Geopolitical Leverage

Conclusion

🌟 India's diplomatic strength must rest not merely on strategic accommodation but on the courage to defend principles, even when powerful partners are uncomfortable.

When the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury on February 28, 2026, President #DonaldTrump initially projected that the conflict would be a rapid campaign lasting four to five weeks. As the fighting dragged into its ninth month, his public timelines repeatedly shifted.

As of today, Sunday, November 15, 2026, 8 months, 2 weeks, and 4 days have elapsed since the 2026 Iran war began. This equals a total duration of 260 days.

Winners and losers so far.

The #UnitedStates and Donald #Trump. LOSER. The U.S. failed to achieve regime change or eliminate Iran's missile and nuclear capabilities. The war cost tens of billions of dollars, depleted air-defense munitions, triggered domestic inflation, and strained trust with Gulf allies. Disruptions in the #StraitOfHormuz and ongoing U.S. naval blockades have kept fuel and borrowing costs elevated nearly nine months into the conflict. #Economy. Severe supply chain and energy shocks from the conflict have pushed wholesale inflation to a nearly four-year high and accelerated grocery and dining costs. Financial markets and policymakers are bracing for prolonged supply-chain and energy friction. Consumer Strain. High fuel, grocery, and borrowing costs have eroded purchasing power for lower- and middle-income households. Shift in Congress. Public dissatisfaction over war-related inflation and cost-of-living pressures played a central role in the November 2026 midterm elections, where Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress and pledged legislative action to end the conflict when they take office in January. Trump is politically weakened. His approval ratings sit near career lows (~32% in recent Reuters/Ipsos and Economist/YouGov polls, with strong disapproval elevated). A Democratic Congress (taking power in January 2027) will have investigatory, budgetary, and legislative tools; polls show ~71% of Americans (including a majority of Republicans) want legislation to end the conflict. Pete #Hegseth faces impeachment pressure over the war. Trump faces pressure to de-escalate further, manage the blockade’s costs, and either force a deal or accept an ongoing low-intensity standoff.

#Iran and Ayatollah Mojtaba #Khamenei. LOSER and WINNER. Despite the assassination of Supreme Leader #AliKhamenei, the destruction of its conventional navy, and over $270 billion in damages, the hardline regime survived under #MojtabaKhamenei. It retained up to 2,500 ballistic missiles and proved it could disrupt global trade via the Strait of #Hormuz.

#Israel and Benjamin #Netanyahu. LOSER. Israel fell short of neutralizing Iran's regional power and was sidelined during U.S. interim truce talks. The conflict eroded bipartisan U.S. public support for Israel and contributed to Prime Minister #BenjaminNetanyahu losing his parliamentary majority in October.

#China and #Xi Jinping, and #Russia and Vladimir #Putin. WINNERS. China expanded its diplomatic standing through ceasefire mediation while securing oil reserves and toll-free vessel passage. Russia gained temporary windfalls from surging global oil prices. Both China and Russia managed to significantly divert the entire world's attention away from their geopolitical tensions, wars, or conflicts with #Taiwan and #Ukraine.

Granny Goodness is a supervillain appearing in American comic books published by DC Comics.[1] She is a New God from Apokolips and a servant of Darkseid who trains others to serve him. Goodness is also the leader of the Female Furies, a group of female warriors from Apokolips.[2]

Goodness has appeared in various media outside comics, primarily in association with Darkseid and the New Gods. Ed Asner, Deborah Strang, and Cloris Leachman, among others, have voiced the character in animation.

Publication history
Granny Goodness first appeared in Mister Miracle #2 (May 1971) and was created by Jack Kirby.[3] Her appearance was modeled after Phyllis Diller.[4]

Fictional character biography
Granny Goodness was originally part of the Lowlies, the oppressed peasant class of Apokolips.[5] She was removed from her parents and trained to be one of Darkseid's elite, the "Hounds". During her training, Goodness is given a guard dog named Mercy, whom she develops a close bond with. Goodness is forced to kill Mercy to become a Hound; Darkseid is impressed and tells Goodness that she has graduated with honors.[3]

After proving herself to be one of Darkseid's elite and most reliable soldiers, Goodness is tasked with running the "Orphanage", a training camp for his minions.[6] Goodness is also the leader of the Female Furies. She raised Highfather's son Scott Free as part of a peace treaty before he escaped from her orphanage, becoming the first person to do so.[7][8]

In the series Amazons Attack!, Granny Goodness poses as Athena, manipulating the Amazons into going to war.[9][3] Goodness also appears in the series Countdown to Final Crisis, where she holds the Olympian Gods prisoner. After the gods are freed by Mary Marvel, Holly Robinson and Harley Quinn, Goodness is attacked and killed by Infinity-Man.[10]

Goodness is reincarnated on Earth, along with the other New Gods, as a member of Darkseid's gang. However, her body is destroyed by Black Alice.[11] In the "Final Crisis" storyline, Goodness takes the body of the Alpha Lantern Kraken and uses it to attack John Stewart and frame Hal Jordan for the assault.[12]
