Promenade des Anglais (French pronunciation: [pʁɔmnad dez‿ɑ̃ɡlɛ], [- dez‿ɑ̃ɡle]; lit. "Walkway of the English"; Niçard: Passejada deis Anglés, Standard Occitan: Passejada dels Anglés) is a promenade along the Mediterranean coast of Nice, France. It extends from Nice Côte d'Azur Airport on the west to the Quai des États-Unis [fr] ("United States Quay") on the east, for a distance of approximately 7 kilometres (4.3 mi).[1] It forms part of Route nationale 98, which runs between Toulon and Menton.

History
Starting in the second half of the 18th century, the English aristocracy took to spending the winter in Nice, enjoying the panorama along the coast. In 1820, when a particularly harsh winter further north brought an influx of beggars to Nice, some of the English proposed that the beggars could work on the construction of a walkway (chemin de promenade) along the sea. It was funded by the Reverend LEWIS Way and members of Holy Trinity, the Anglican church in Nice.[2][3]

The city of Nice, intrigued by the prospect of a pleasant promenade, greatly increased the scope of the work. The Promenade was first called the Camin deis Anglés (the English Way) by the Niçois in their native dialect. After the annexation of Nice by France in 1860 it was rechristened La Promenade des Anglais.

The Promenade was the site of the team time trial in the 2013 Tour de France, held on 2 July 2013. It was also featured as a start and finish location of the first two stages of the 2020 Tour de France.[4] Due to the Paris Olympics, the 2024 Tour de France concluded on the Promenade, instead of its usual location of the Champs-Élysées.[5]

Stages 8 and 9 of the 2026 Tour de France Femmes concluded on the Promenade.[6]

Modern day
For local inhabitants, Promenade des Anglais has simply become the Promenade or, for short, La Prom. It is popular with bicyclists, baby strollers, and families, especially on Sundays. It has also become a favorite place for skateboarders and in-line skaters.

2016 Bastille Day attack
Main article: 2016 Nice truck attack
On 14 July 2016, a truck was deliberately driven at revellers celebrating Bastille Day on the Promenade. The driver, 31-year-old Mohamed Lahouaiej-Bouhlel,[7] also shot at others before crossing the road in the vehicle to continue the assault. The vehicle was surrounded by police near the Palais de la Méditerranée, and the terrorist was shot dead. Eighty-six people were killed, and 458 were wounded.[8]

Primary Germanic and Norman Origin
Frankish Roots: It stems from the Old Frankish Hlūtwīg (or Chlodowech), composed of hlūt ("loud" or "fame") and wīg ("battle" or "war").
Latin and French Evolution: The name was Latinized as Ludovicus, evolved into Old French as Clovis or Louis, and was brought to Britain by the Normans after 1066 as Lowis or Lewis.

All historians acknowledge the ascendancy of the popes began in 308 A.D., when King Clovis of the Salian or Merovingian Franks (later France), won the decisive battle in the Catholic and Arian religious war, thereby settling the dispute in favor of the Catholics. But the popes' temporal reign officially began in the year 538 A.D. when Roman Emperor Justinian subdued the last of the three kingdoms, or "horns," that opposed the rise of the Papacy.

Promenade des Anglais (French pronunciation: [pʁɔmnad dez‿ɑ̃ɡlɛ], [- dez‿ɑ̃ɡle]; lit. "Walkway of the English"; Niçard: Passejada deis Anglés, Standard Occitan: Passejada dels Anglés) is a promenade along the Mediterranean coast of Nice, France. It extends from Nice Côte d'Azur Airport on the west to the Quai des États-Unis [fr] ("United States Quay") on the east, for a distance of approximately 7 kilometres (4.3 mi).[1] It forms part of Route nationale 98, which runs between Toulon and Menton.

History
Starting in the second half of the 18th century, the English aristocracy took to spending the winter in Nice, enjoying the panorama along the coast. In 1820, when a particularly harsh winter further north brought an influx of beggars to Nice, some of the English proposed that the beggars could work on the construction of a walkway (chemin de promenade) along the sea. It was funded by the Reverend LEWIS Way and members of Holy Trinity, the Anglican church in Nice.[2][3]

The city of Nice, intrigued by the prospect of a pleasant promenade, greatly increased the scope of the work. The Promenade was first called the Camin deis Anglés (the English Way) by the Niçois in their native dialect. After the annexation of Nice by France in 1860 it was rechristened La Promenade des Anglais.

The Promenade was the site of the team time trial in the 2013 Tour de France, held on 2 July 2013. It was also featured as a start and finish location of the first two stages of the 2020 Tour de France.[4] Due to the Paris Olympics, the 2024 Tour de France concluded on the Promenade, instead of its usual location of the Champs-Élysées.[5]

Stages 8 and 9 of the 2026 Tour de France Femmes concluded on the Promenade.[6]

Modern day
For local inhabitants, Promenade des Anglais has simply become the Promenade or, for short, La Prom. It is popular with bicyclists, baby strollers, and families, especially on Sundays. It has also become a favorite place for skateboarders and in-line skaters.

2016 Bastille Day attack
Main article: 2016 Nice truck attack
On 14 July 2016, a truck was deliberately driven at revellers celebrating Bastille Day on the Promenade. The driver, 31-year-old Mohamed Lahouaiej-Bouhlel,[7] also shot at others before crossing the road in the vehicle to continue the assault. The vehicle was surrounded by police near the Palais de la Méditerranée, and the terrorist was shot dead. Eighty-six people were killed, and 458 were wounded.[8]

Primary Germanic and Norman Origin
Frankish Roots: It stems from the Old Frankish Hlūtwīg (or Chlodowech), composed of hlūt ("loud" or "fame") and wīg ("battle" or "war").
Latin and French Evolution: The name was Latinized as Ludovicus, evolved into Old French as Clovis or Louis, and was brought to Britain by the Normans after 1066 as Lowis or Lewis.

All historians acknowledge the ascendancy of the popes began in 308 A.D., when King Clovis of the Salian or Merovingian Franks (later France), won the decisive battle in the Catholic and Arian religious war, thereby settling the dispute in favor of the Catholics. But the popes' temporal reign officially began in the year 538 A.D. when Roman Emperor Justinian subdued the last of the three kingdoms, or "horns," that opposed the rise of the Papacy.

3 [d]So he carried me away into the wilderness in the Spirit, and I saw a woman sit upon a [e]scarlet colored beast, full of names of blasphemy, which had seven heads, and ten horns.

4 And [f]the woman was arrayed [g]in purple and scarlet, and gilded with gold, and precious stones, and pearls, [h]and had a cup of gold in her hand full of abomination, and filthiness of her fornication.

5 [i]And in her forehead was a name written, A mystery, [j]that great Babylon that mother of whoredoms, and abominations of the earth.

6 [k]And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of Saints, and with the blood of the Martyrs of JESUS: and when I saw her, [l]I wondered with great marvel.

7 [m]Then the Angel said unto me, Wherefore marvelest thou? I will show thee the mystery of that woman, and of that beast that beareth her, which hath seven heads and ten horns.

8 [n]The beast that thou hast seen, [o]was and is not, and [p]shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and shall go into perdition, and they that dwell on the earth, shall wonder (whose names are not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world) [q]when they behold the beast that was, and is not, and yet is.

9 [r]Here is the mind that hath wisdom, The [s]seven heads [t]are seven mountains, whereon the woman sitteth: [u]they are also seven Kings.

10 [v]Five are fallen, [w]and one is, [x]and another is not yet come: and when he cometh, he must continue a short space.

11 [y]And the beast that was, and is not, is even [z]the eighth, and is [aa]one of the seven, and [ab]all go into destruction.

12 [ac]And the ten horns which thou sawest, are [ad]ten kings, which yet have not received a kingdom, but shall receive power, as Kings [ae]at one hour with the beast.

13 [af]These have one mind, and shall give their power and authority unto the beast.

14 These shall fight with the [ag]Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of Lords, and King of Kings: and they that are on his side, called, and chosen, and faithful.

15 [ah]And he said unto me, The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, [ai]are people, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.

16 And the ten [aj]horns which thou sawest upon the beast, are they that shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate, and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.

17 [ak]For God hath put in their hearts to fulfill his will, and to do with one consent for to give their kingdom unto the beast, until the words of God be fulfilled.

18 And that woman which thou sawest, is that [al]great city which reigned over the kings of the earth.

Revelation 17:1 The state of the Church militant being declared, now followeth the state of the Church overcoming and getting victory, as I showed before in the beginning of chapter 10. The state is set forth in 4 chapters. As in the place beforegoing I noted, that in that history the order of time was not always exactly observed, so the same is to be understood in this history, that it is distinguished according to the persons of which it treateth, and that in the several stories of the persons is severly observed in the time thereof. For first is delivered the story of Babylon destroyed, in this and the next chap. (for this Babylon out of all doubt shall perish before the 2 beasts and the Dragon). Secondly is delivered the destruction of both the two beasts, chap. 19. And lastly of the Dragon, chap. 20, in the story of the spiritual Babylon are distinctly set forth the state thereof in this chap. and the overthrow done from God, chap. 18. In this verse and that which followeth is a transition or passage unto the first argument, consisting of a particular calling of the Prophet (as often heretofore) and a general proposition.
Revelation 17:1 That is the damnable harlot, by a figure of speech called hypallage. For S. John as yet had not seen her. Although another interpretation may be borne, yet I like this better.
Revelation 17:1 The sentence that is pronounced against this harlot.
Revelation 17:3 Henceforth is propounded the type of Babylon, and the state thereof in 4 verses. After a declaration of the type, in the rest of this chap., in the type are described two things, the beast (of whom chap. 13), in verse 3, and the woman that sitteth upon the beast, verses 4, 5, 6. The beast in process of time hath gotten somewhat more than was expressed in the former vision. First in that it is not read before that he was appareled in scarlet, a robe imperial and of triumph. Secondly, in that this is full of names of blasphemy: the other carried the name of blasphemy only in his head. So God did teach that this beast is much increased in impiety and injustice and doth in this last age, triumph in both these more insolently and proudly than ever before.
Revelation 17:3 A scarlet color, that is, with a red and purple garment: and surely it was not without cause that the Romish clergy were so much delighted with this color.
Revelation 17:4 That harlot, the spiritual Babylon, which is Rome. She is described by her attire, profession and deeds.
Revelation 17:4 In attire most glorious, triumphant, most rich, and most gorgeous.
Revelation 17:4 In profession, the nourisher of all, in this verse, and teaching her mysteries unto all, verse 5, setting forth all things most magnificently: but indeed most pernicious besotting miserable men with her cup, and bringing upon them a deadly giddiness.
Revelation 17:5 Deceiving with the title of religion, and public inscription of mystery: which the beast in times past did not bear.
Revelation 17:5 An exposition: in which S. John declareth what manner of woman this is.
Revelation 17:6 In manner of deeds: She is red with blood, and sheddeth it most licentiously, and therefore is colored with the blood of the Saints, as on the contrary part. Christ is set forth imbrued with the blood of his enemies; Isa. 3:1.
Revelation 17:6 A passage unto the second part of this chapter, by occasion given of S. John, as the words of the Angel do show, in the next verse.
Revelation 17:7 The second part or place, as I said, verse 1. The narration of the vision, promised in this verse, and delivered in the verse following. Now there is delivered first a narration of the beast and his story, unto verse 14. After, of the harlot, unto the end of the chap.
Revelation 17:8 The story of the beast hath a triple description of him. The first is a distinction of this beast from all that ever hath been at any time: which distinction is contained in this verse: The second is a delineation or painting out of the beast by things present, by which he might even at that time be known of the godly, and this delineation is according to his heads, verses 2, 10, 11. The third is an historical foretelling of things to come, and to be done by him: and these are ascribed unto his horns, verses 12, 13, 14. This beast is that Empire of Rome, of which I spake, chap. 13:11, according to the mutations and changes whereof which then had already happened, the holy Ghost hath distinguished and set out the same. The Apostle distinguisheth this beast from all others in these words. The beast which thou sawest, was and is not. For so I expound the words of the Apostle for evidence’s sake as I will further declare in the notes following.
Revelation 17:8 The meaning is, that beast which thou sawest before (Rev. 13:1) and which yet thou hast now seen, was, (I say was) even from Julius Caesar in respect of beginning, rising up, station, glory, dominion, manner and stock, from the house of Julius: and yet is not now the same, if thou look unto the house and stock for the dominion of this family was translated unto another, after the death of Nero from the other unto a third, from a third unto a fourth, and so forth was varied and altered by innumerable changes. Finally, the Empire is one, as it were one beast: but exceedingly varied by kindreds, families, and persons. It was therefore (saith S. John) in the kindred or house of Julius: and now it is not in that kindred, but translated unto another.
Revelation 17:8 As if he should say, Also the same that is, shall shortly not be: but shall ascend out of the depth, or out of the sea (as was said, Rev. 13:1) that is, shall be a new stock from amongst the nations without difference, and shall in the same state go unto destruction or ruin, and perish: and so shall successively new Princes or Emperors come and go, arise and fall, the body of the beast remaining still, but tossed with so many and often alterations, as no man can but marvel that this beast was able to stand and hold out, in so many mutations. Verily no Empire that ever was tossed with so many changes, and as it were with so many tempests of the sea, ever continued so long.
Revelation 17:8 That is as many as have not learned the providence of God, according to the faith of the Saints, shall marvel at these grievous and often changes when they shall consider, the selfsame beast, which is the Roman Empire, to have been, not to be, and to be and still molested with perpetual mutation, and yet in the same to stand and continue. This in mine opinion is the most simple exposition of this place, and confirmed by the event of the things themselves. Although by the last change also, by which the Empire, that before was civil became Ecclesiastical, is not obscurely signified by these words: of which two, the first exercised cruelty upon the bodies of the saints: the other also upon their souls: the first by human order and policy, the other under the color of the law of God, and of Religion, raged and imbrued itself with the blood of the godly.
Revelation 17:9 An exhortation preparing unto audience, by the same argument, with that of Christ: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear. Wherefore, for mine own part, I had rather read in this place, Let there be here a mind, etc. So the Angel passeth fully unto the second place of this description.
Revelation 17:9 Very children know what that seven hilled city is, which is so much spoken of, and whereof Virgil thus reporteth, And compasseth seven towers in one wall: that city it is, which when John wrote these things had rule over the kings of the earth: It was and is not, and yet it remaineth this day, but it is declining to destruction.
Revelation 17:9 This is the painting out of the beast by things present (as I said before) whereby S. John endeavored to describe the same, that he might both be known of the godly in that age, and be further observed and marked of posterity afterwards. This delineation hath one type, that is, his heads, but a double description or application of the type: one permanent from the nature of itself, the other changeable, by the working of men. The description permanent, is by the seven hills, in this verse, the other that fleeteth, is from the seven kings, verses 10, 11. And here it is worthy to be observed, that one type hath sometimes two or more applications, as seemeth good unto the holy Ghost to express either one thing by divers types, or divers things by one type. So I noted before, of the seven spirits, Rev. 1:4. Now this woman that sitteth upon seven hills, is the city of Rome, called in times past of the Greeks, … i. of seven tops or crests, and of Varro, septiceps, i. of her seven heads (as here) of seven heads, and of others, septicollis, i. standing upon seven hills.

text:
At 9 this morning in Fincastle, Virginia, the main arguments begin in the Botetourt County data center case. The question in front of Judge Michael Doucette sounds narrow. It is not.

Can a county approve a $3 billion project in a closed session it never properly described, and then make that approval stick by building fast enough that no court wants to unwind it?

Start with what is not in dispute. On June 24, 2025, the Botetourt County Board of Supervisors went into closed session citing economic development involving the Amsterdam District. The notice named no performance agreement and no data center. Hours later the board reconvened, and the county announced that Google, through its subsidiary Helio Capital, had bought 312 acres at the Greenfield industrial park for $14.06 million to build three data center buildings totaling about 921,000 square feet. The performance agreement promises at least 150 jobs at a median salary of at least $86,000 if the first building is finished by 2030.

Robert Dallas, a retired anesthesiologist who lives about 2,600 feet from the site, sued on November 2 under Virginia's Freedom of Information Act. His argument is about the sequence. FOIA lets a board discuss a deal behind closed doors. It still requires the board to reasonably identify the substance of what it is about to discuss before the door closes. Dallas's lawyer, John Fishwick, told the court last Tuesday there was nothing in the notices about a data center, and he played the livestream of the vote itself: "They can't later say what they were voting on."

The county's answer has two layers, and the second one matters more than the first. The first is legal: the notices were specific enough, the project was described in detail in open session within hours, and closed-door negotiation is how competitive deals get done. The second is practical, and county counsel Julian Harf said it plainly: "We are 16 months down the road. Things have been done that can't be undone."

The record supports the second sentence, which is exactly why it deserves scrutiny. County officials testified last week that Helio Capital has already paid $2.5 million of its $4 million community pledge to the Economic Development Authority, much of it spent, plus about $1 million of the land-sale proceeds. Mass grading has commenced at Greenfield. Permits for the site plan, land disturbance, and contractor trailers were issued from late August through late September, and construction continues today. Every dollar spent and every acre graded strengthens the argument that voiding the agreement would now be inequitable, whatever happened in that closed session.

That is the incentive underneath this entire fight, and it extends well beyond one Virginia county. If spending quickly enough converts a disclosure violation into a sunk cost a court will not touch, then the lesson for every locality courting a hyperscale campus is straightforward: sign first, announce the same afternoon, break ground before anyone can file. The disclosure law still exists. It just arrives after the tractors.

Doucette has already ruled once. On November 10 he overruled the demurrer, finding the claims sufficient to proceed, and he took the defense's plea in bar, the argument that Dallas filed too late, under advisement. That timeliness question is still open this morning: the defense counts 16 months from the vote; Fishwick counts a filing inside the two-year window the law allows. The judge also disclosed, before any of it, that his wife holds Alphabet stock amounting to less than one percent of their portfolio. He put it on the record himself. In a case about what gets disclosed and when, that detail is worth noticing.

What Dallas is asking for is the strongest remedy FOIA offers: declare the performance agreement void, rescind everything done under it since June 24, 2025, and run the process again in compliance with the law, with the defendants paying costs and fees. Fishwick's version was shorter in court: "The way you fix a FOIA violation is you have to re-vote."

Today's hearing is where the evidence on compliance gets heard. I will post what the judge does with it when there is a ruling to report.

‘RTE advertised over 250 roles in less than two years, the Irish Mail on Sunday has learned.
Documents that were accessed via a Freedom of Information (Fol) request show that the cash-strapped broadcaster has advertised for multiple positions from the beginning of last year to the end of September this year - filling over 230 of them.
Nineteen of these are new roles, RTE this week confirmed - with a spokesman saying that over 90 per cent of the jobs were replacing existing roles.
Just 68 have exited through its Voluntary Exit Programme (VEP) in the same time period. The slow pace of the VEP roll-out was cited by Media Minister Patrick O'Donovan last month as one of the reasons he was withholding €20million of the €260milliom promised to RTÉ in State funding next year.
The new figures show that, while the national broadcaster was publicly committing to massive job cuts, it has continued to recruit staff.
Between January 1, 2025, and September 25 of this year, of the 255 RTÉ posts that were advertised, nearly half - some 114 - offered permanent jobs.’

The Dejika document of American Surrender, written 3/17/26:

We, the American people, acknowledge that we have committed a flagrant breach of international law in initiating this war against you. The carelessness of this decision only exacerbates its severity as an error.

Our recent administration has done nothing but made a mockery of the aspirations of mutual respect that are the foundation of our vision of a just international community. This may be a reflection of an accurate—if brutish—acknowledgement of reality: for many years, if not forever, the aspirations of our international community have been just that or worse, cynical theater deployed to violent ends.

It is my firm belief, as a proud American, that there is a true kernel of sincerity in our nation’s many decades of rhetoric regarding the importance of international and humanitarian law. This grave error, this war of aggression fueled by nothing but ego, offers us Americans a chance to do something remarkable. We can demonstrate to the world that, deep down, we mean what we say. We can admit we are wrong, and we can take responsibility.

To that end, I have an offer of peace. These are our terms:

First, the United States and Israel will acknowledge the illegality of this war. As part of taking responsibility, we will agree to pay reparations for the damage our militaries have inflicted on your country. Likewise, we will submit any domestic review of alleged warcrimes to an international body for audit and consent to their ultimate jurisdiction.

Second, we will make significant concessions towards ensuring your security and sovereignty.

A) We will acknowledge your need to develop nuclear weapons. While our hope is for a lasting regime of non-proliferation, it is a fact that an aggressive regional rival, with a demonstrable history of refusal to comply with international law or norms, possesses nuclear capabilities. Until this fact changes, your security demands reciprocal deterrence. Should this rival decide to dismantle their nuclear weapons program, and to submit to a rigorous international process to ensure that it was completed and never restarted, we would then expect you to do the same. Further, should your rival not agree to these terms, our government will seek to apply maximum economic and diplomatic pressure on them to do so, including the suspension of military support and sale of equipment.

B) We cannot abandon our military bases in the Gulf. As a point of principle, it is the sovereign decision of the host-states to determine their status. As a point of practice, they are a vital node in our own security infrastructure. It is our hope, that in offering these terms, we can begin to rebuild faith that our security infrastructure is not a malicious one. To aid this rebuilding of trust, we are willing to offer you the ability to station advisors at our regional bases to be able to monitor their activities on the ground.

C) We are willing to make concessions regarding the status of your regional allies. In Lebanon, we propose a joint American-Iranian effort to disarm Hezbollah while allowing them to participate in the operations of the formal Lebanese state. Should this party aim to capture the Lebanese state to pursue policies of regional aggression, we reserve the right to intervene. In Iraq, we are willing to end our campaign of political pressure against Iranian influence in the national government. It is up for the Iraqis to decide what their foreign policy should be. However, should this government aim to dispossess its Kurdish constituents in the north, we reserve the right to intervene. We believe that the political situation in Yemen is complicated enough that it should not be subject to these bilateral negotiations, but discussed by a broader international community. Finally, although we deeply regret the circumstances that have brought us here, we will commit to applying maximum pressure to achieve the establishment of a viable Palestinian state—pressure that would be identical to that identified above regarding nuclear disarmament.

D) As a sign of future goodwill, our countries will work on not merely affirming peace but affirming friendship. As the offending party, we acknowledge that any such effort would require meaningful apologies on our part, and we will have a discussion as a nation as to what those should be, though they would likely take the form of investment beyond reparations alongside cultural and intellectual exchange. While we cannot oblige you to accept these material expressions of our regret, we hope you might consider it.

E) Regarding the Strait of Hormuz, it must be restored to the status quo ante as an area of free and unfettered navigation. As we will lift all sanctions regarding your nuclear weapons program per our 2A acknowledgement of it as your right, your energy exports will continue to flow freely after we achieve peace. We cannot accept an Iranian claim of sovereignty to that water way. We may have forced you to demonstrate your capability in that regard, and we do not fault you for it. But ceding the principle of freedom of navigation sets a precedent that could upset the fundamental aims of this peace offering: reaffirming the US commitment to international norms and laws.

~

Our nations share a revolutionary heritage. American foreign policy has, for many decades now, lost sight of the principles and virtues that our own revolutionary founders once held regarding the rights of people and their governments. We have enabled a criminal regime to take their place. It is to our great detriment, and we owe more than a sentimental apology to not only you, but to our allies and our global neighbors.

Exceptionalism is gauche, it is true. But if it can be built on a foundation of humility—a humility that lies at the heart of this offer of peace—perhaps the US can once again be a state worth emulating, and for the right reasons.

With deep regret,

The American People

*MAPHISA, MATABELELAND SOUTH | 14 NOVEMBER 2026 –* The *Patriotic Entrepreneurs League (PEL)* has reaffirmed its commitment to youth empowerment, grassroots development and community-centred social responsibility through its active participation and material support at the *Vice President Mohadi Annual Tournament and Youth Sports Expo* held in *Maphisa, Matabeleland South.*

Held under the theme *“Empowering Drug-Free Youths for Vision 2030,”* the sporting event brought together political leadership, Government representatives, sports stakeholders and community participants, with the Guest of Honour being the Vice President of the Republic of Zimbabwe, *Rtd Colonel Dr. K.C.D. Mohadi.*

PEL’s participation transcended institutional visibility, reflecting a practical commitment to initiatives that leverage sport as a vehicle for youth development, social cohesion and the prevention of drug and substance abuse.

A notable highlight of the organisation’s participation was its tangible contribution to the sporting programme. PEL donated training kits for both netball and football teams, alongside sporting balls, in support of grassroots sports development and the nurturing of emerging talent. These contributions reinforce PEL’s understanding that meaningful youth empowerment must extend beyond rhetoric; it requires deliberate investment in opportunities, resources and platforms through which young people can discover, develop and realise their potential.

The PEL delegation comprised its Matabeleland South leadership, including *PEL Matabeleland South Vice Chairperson Cde Lindani Nyathi, Provincial Chairperson Cde Ntokozo Ngwenya* and *Provincial Secretary-General Cde Nozie Mabhikwa,* alongside *PEL Bulawayo Metropolitan Provincial Chairperson Cde Mayibongwe Moyo* and *Cde Coliett Sesedza, PEL Bulawayo Provincial Secretary-General* amongst other members.

In a further expression of institutional identity, recognition and engagement, PEL presented its organisational regalia to Vice President Mohadi and the Provincial leadership, symbolising the organisation’s growing institutional presence and commitment to constructive engagement with national and provincial leadership.

The event was also graced by the Minister of Sport, Recreation, Arts and Culture, *Hon. Cde A. Sanyatwe,* a former Commander of the Zimbabwe National Army. His presence underscored the significance of sport as an instrument for national development, youth engagement and social transformation.

Also in attendance was the Minister of State for Provincial Affairs and Devolution for Matabeleland South, *Hon. A. Ngulube,* who engaged meaningfully with the PEL delegation, creating an important opportunity for interaction and dialogue around shared developmental interests.

The tournament culminated in the recognition of outstanding sporting performances, with victorious teams receiving medals and trophies in acknowledgement of their achievements. Beyond the competitive spectacle, the awards celebrated discipline, teamwork, determination and the positive values that organised sport can cultivate among young people.

PEL’s engagement in Maphisa reflects a broader appreciation that Zimbabwe’s Vision 2030 aspirations cannot be realised through economic programmes alone. Investment in human capital, particularly the country’s youthful population, remains equally fundamental to sustainable national development.

The fight against drug and substance abuse demands coordinated action involving Gvt, communities, sporting institutions, civil society and development-oriented organisations. By supporting sporting initiatives and providing essential equipment, PEL is contributing to the creation of constructive alternatives that encourage young people to channel their energy, creativity and ambitions towards productive pursuits.

text:
One of the mysterious events and archives of Chinese historical figures

Case 1: Emperor Qin Shi Huang - Sent 3,000 boys and girls to search for the elixir of immortality
Person: Emperor Qin Shi Huang
Time: 3rd century BC
Key words: Immortality, Fairy Mountain, Xu Fu, Mysterious Voyage Eastward

- After unifying the six states, Emperor Qin Shi Huang had almost unparalleled power but still couldn't shake off a fear: death;
- It is said that he sent Xu Fu, leading 3,000 boys and girls, carrying food, craftsmen and various supplies, to sail out to sea to search for the three immortal mountains in the East Sea, namely Penglai, Fangtang and Yingzhou, where the immortals lived and possessed the magical medicine that could make people live forever;
- However, Xu Fu never returned; it is said that Xu Fu reached Japan and some places there still retain the legend of Xu Fu and related memorial sites.

Confirmed
The story of Emperor Qin Shi Huang's pursuit of immortality and Xu Fu's quest for immortality are recorded in "Records of the Grand Historian".

Case 2: Emperor Yongzheng - Died suddenly, was it really killed by Lu Siumiang?
Person: Emperor Yongzheng
Time: 1735
Key words: Sudden death, Palace assassination, Magic Pills, Lu Siumiang

- Emperor Yongzheng died suddenly in Jiuzhengyan in the Yuanmingyuan at the age of 58;
Legend 1: Lu Siumiang entered the palace to assassinate Emperor Yongzheng;
Legend 2: Poisoned by magic pills;
Legend 3: Palace internal murder.

Confirmed
There are archival records of Emperor Yongzheng's activities related to alchemy in his later years.

Case 3: Emperor Jianwen - Disappeared mysteriously after the Great Fire of Nanjing Palace
Person: Emperor Jianwen Zhu Yunwen
Time: 1402
Key words: Palace fire, disappearance, Monk, Seclusion, Secret Search

- Emperor Jianwen was the grandson of Zhu Yuanzhang. After ascending the throne, he attempted to weaken the power of the various vassal kings but thus clashed with his uncle Zhu Di, who later became Emperor Wanli. This war was called the "Jingran Rebellion".
- In 1402, Zhu Di invaded Nanjing and a palace fire broke out. Emperor Jianwen disappeared thereafter;

The three most famous escape theories:
1: Became a monk;
2: Escaped to Yunnan;
3: Escaped to Ningde, Fujian

French football star Franck Ribéry publicly admitted that he has Chinese royal blood and is a descendant of Emperor Jianwen Zhu Yunwen of the Ming Dynasty. His ancestors fled to Persia after Zhu Di seized the throne and later moved to France.

Case 4: Liu Bovin - Legend of being able to predict history hundreds of years in advance
Person: Liu Bovin (Liu Ji)
Time: 14th century
Key words: Prediction, Ingenious Calculation, "Bread Song"

- Liu Bovin was an important advisor to the founding of the Ming Dynasty. Later, he was gradually portrayed as a mysterious figure who could predict the future, be proficient in astronomy and geography, and even understand the secrets of heaven.
- The popular version claims that it predicted the downfall of the Ming Dynasty, the rise of the Qing Dynasty, and even more recent historical events.

Case 5: Emperor Chongzheng - The Ancient Elm Tree on Jingshan and the Last Night of the Ming Dynasty
Person: Emperor Chongzheng Zhu Youjian
Time: 1644
Key words: National Collapse, Ancient Elm Tree, Testament, Palace Tragedy

- In 1644, Beijing fell and Li Zicheng's army invaded Beijing. The Ming Dynasty was on the verge of collapse. Emperor Chongzheng was in a desperate situation in the palace;
- Emperor Chongzheng hanged himself in Jingshan at the age of 33; the eunuch Wang Cheng'en also committed suicide.
- There were crying sounds at night in Jingshan, the shadow of the ancient tree and the ghosts did not disappear.

ANTHROPIC IPO PRIME PUBLIC ROUND CLOSES TOMORROW! ARE YOU STILL CONSIDERING GETTING EXPOSURE TO $ANT? 🧐

After weeks of covering Anthropic's upcoming IPO, we are now approaching one of the more important dates for anyone considering participating.

November 17, 08:00 UTC.

That's the scheduled deadline for Bitget IPO Prime's Public Round, assuming Anthropic proceeds with its anticipated November 19 listing.

And before that deadline arrives, I want to revisit one reason Anthropic has attracted so much investor attention.

LET'S TALK ABOUT ANTHROPIC'S BUSINESS GROWTH 🌱

According to its recent IPO filing, Anthropic generated about $33.2 billion in revenue in the first nine months of 2026, up 1,206% from the same period last year.

That's a substantial increase for a company founded just five years ago.

Much of the attention surrounding the company comes from Claude and its growing presence in enterprise AI through developer tools, coding assistants, and business applications.

But I would not look at revenue growth alone when evaluating the company.

Anthropic is also spending enormous amounts of money on computing infrastructure, and maintaining that growth will require continued investment.

For me, one angle to look at is whether the company can eventually turn its rapidly growing revenue into sustainable profits without increasing infrastructure spending at the same pace.

And given the selloff in tech stocks recently, investors will be paying close attention to that balance.

WHAT ABOUT THE DEMAND FOR ITS IPO? 🙋

Recent reports suggest that Anthropic's offering has attracted demand several times greater than the shares expected to be available (6x-7x oversubscribed).

That suggests institutional interest remains strong, but it does not mean Anthropic is guaranteed to pump significantly once trading begins.

A heavily subscribed IPO can still disappoint investors if the final valuation is too high or broader market conditions deteriorate.

That's why I would pay more attention to Anthropic's final offering price and valuation than assume the enthusiasm surrounding AI will continue after listing.

FOR THOSE CONSIDERING BITGET IPO PRIME 🔎

The Public Round remains open to eligible users, allowing commitments between $100 and $25,000 using USDT or USDGO.

A 5% underwriting service fee applies to the amount actually allocated, and allocations are calculated proportionally based on the available pool.

Participants will receive rANT, a tokenized asset linked to Anthropic, rather than direct ownership of the company's shares.

And if you are new to @Bitget, there's also a separate promotional campaign offering additional rANT rewards.

Eligible new users who registered from November 2 can qualify for 20 USDT worth of rANT after making a qualifying first deposit of at least 1,000 USDT and participating in the IPO subscription.

A higher reward tier offers 100 USDT worth of rANT for a qualifying first deposit of at least 30,000 USDT, with an additional 5 USDT available for eligible P2P deposits.

These rewards are subject to registration, a limited 100,000 USDT reward pool, and a fund-retention requirement extending 30 days after the IPO. The two main reward tiers cannot be combined.

SO, WOULD I STILL CONSIDER ANTHROPIC AT THIS STAGE? 💭

In my own opinion, given the negative sentiment and recent sell-off in the crypto market, the situation reminds me of what happened ahead of the SpaceX IPO five months ago.

I would not be surprised if some traders were already selling their crypto holdings a few days ago to free up capital for Anthropic. It may not make sense to everyone, but markets do not always need to make sense.

Sometimes, money simply moves from one opportunity to another, and right now, Anthropic seems to be getting a lot of attention despite everything happening in the broader market.

Of course, that does not mean the company will perform the same way SpaceX did. But considering the demand we have seen so far, I think it's still worth looking into before the Public Round closes.

For anyone who's planning to get exposure to Anthropic before the Public Round closes, here's the official campaign page: https://t.co/TDxg4gOIFs

Remember that November 19 remains an anticipated IPO date, and the subscription timeline may change.

rANT does not provide direct shareholder ownership, voting rights, or direct dividends. The token can trade below its reference offering price, and returns or allocations are not assured.

Make sure you understand the product terms and risks before committing capital. This is not financial advice.

My question for everyone following the Anthropic IPO is, are you more interested in its extraordinary revenue growth, or are you concerned that its valuation might already reflect years of future AI expansion?

text:
🥚 Have you ever wondered if there are any engineering Easter eggs hiding in plain sight during Starship's historic tower catch? 🔥

The physics alone was incredible, but there's more to this story 🔥

Let's start with something the spectacular landing footage barely shows: how Starship actually makes contact with the tower.

🎯 The mechanical capture interface is surprisingly small

Ship 42 wasn't caught by wrapping the chopsticks tightly around its massive stainless-steel body.

Instead, two small structural fittings near its upper section provide the contact points where the tower supports the spacecraft's weight.

According to Ars Technica's firsthand reporting from Starbase, each fitting extends only about a foot from the vehicle.

Just getting those two tiny fittings lined up is an engineering challenge of its own.

Starship has to approach with tightly controlled lateral movement, attitude, and descent speed so those fittings meet the tower's support surfaces in exactly the right position.

Any major misalignment or excess movement at contact could put enormous structural stress on both the spacecraft and the tower.

But Starship isn't the only machine that needs precise control.

SpaceX also redesigned Pad 2's chopsticks for the V3 generation.

The new arms are shorter, allowing them to move faster and better track incoming vehicles. SpaceX also switched their main actuators from hydraulic to electromechanical systems for better speed, redundancy, and reliability.

That means the spacecraft and the tower have separate, closely coordinated jobs.

Starship's flight computers have to guide the vehicle into the capture envelope, while the tower's actuators position the chopsticks to receive it.

As the fittings settle onto the support surfaces and the landing engines shut down, the spacecraft's weight transfers into the tower's structure.

And getting those two contact points into position starts long before the landing burn.

🧭 Starship and Super Heavy approach the tower from different directions

During a standard tower recovery, Super Heavy performs a boostback burn right after separation, reversing course and heading back toward Starbase from over the Gulf.

Starship takes a completely different trajectory.

After reentering over the Pacific, Ship 42 crossed Baja and northern Mexico before approaching South Texas from the west.

But why did its return path have to cross land in the first place?

SpaceX's Lars Blackmore explained that getting back to the eastern coast of Texas from orbit meant flying across the continent. The team therefore designed the route to pass mostly over desert and weave around towns, keeping the population beneath the spacecraft as low as possible.

As Ship 42 approached South Texas, it passed north of South Padre Island and headed offshore over the Gulf of Mexico.

From there, Starship performed a sweeping final turn back toward Starbase, a maneuver SpaceX calls a "swoosh."

That turn is especially interesting because it brought Starship around to approach the tower from the Gulf side, rather than following Super Heavy's usual return direction.

And simply reaching the right coordinates isn't enough.

The spacecraft also needs tightly controlled heading, attitude, and lateral movement for the final landing maneuver. The return path and tower approach have to work together.

SpaceX's V3 redesign also introduced upgraded multi-sensor navigation, built specifically for high-precision autonomous flight with greater redundancy.

All of this helps Starship arrive at the tower in the right position and state of motion for capture.

And even the sharpest guidance system can't pull off a catch if the engines aren't ready when Starship arrives.

❄️ Starship must restart its engines after nearly a day in space

Super Heavy's recovery happens within minutes of launch.

Starship's propulsion system has to stay operational throughout a much longer orbital mission, which brings major challenges with cryogenic propellant storage, thermal management, tank pressure, and reliable engine restarts.

Starship runs on liquid oxygen and liquid methane, and both have to stay properly conditioned despite heat entering the propellant system during an extended stay in orbit.

Microgravity complicates things even further because liquid propellants don't naturally settle at the bottom of their tanks like they do on Earth.

That makes propellant management critical before an in-orbit engine restart.

SpaceX's V3 redesign includes several upgrades built specifically to support long-duration flights.

These include fully vacuum-jacketed header-tank feed lines, electrically actuated cryogenic recirculation, upgraded reaction-control systems, and dedicated hardware to manage how cryogenic propellants interact with the engines during long coast phases.

Together, these systems help maintain the propellant conditions needed for critical burns long after liftoff.

Flight 15 put this to the test with two recovery-critical engine restarts under very different conditions.

A single Raptor successfully restarted more than 21 hours after liftoff to perform the deorbit burn.

Later, after surviving atmospheric reentry, three sea-level Raptors lit up for the final landing maneuver.

The first burn established Starship's return trajectory. The second provided the thrust needed to flip the ship upright, stabilize its descent, and line up those small structural fittings for capture.

Both relied on a propulsion system capable of reliable ignition and precise thrust control nearly a full day after launch.

But even with a healthy spacecraft and an accurate return path, the catch wasn't guaranteed.

🛡️ The catch depended on an extensive flight-safety system

This might be one of the most overlooked parts of Flight 15.

And the safety checks started long before Starship returned to Earth.

After deploying its Starlink satellites, Ship 42 slowly rotated so a camera aboard one of the newly released satellites could inspect its heat shield.

In total, three of the 26 Starlink V3 satellites carried cameras designed to photograph the spacecraft and transmit those images back to operators.

Ground-based tracking cameras provided another perspective.

It's a fascinating arrangement. Starship had just delivered those satellites to orbit, and they were already helping engineers assess the condition of the spacecraft that launched them.

The images became part of the evidence SpaceX used to determine whether Ship 42 was healthy enough to return to Starbase.

And the decision involved much more than examining the heat shield.

SpaceX built three scheduled return checks into the mission.

The first offered an early return opportunity near Hawaii. The second provided a backup splashdown zone several hundred kilometers off the coast of Chile. The third offered another Pacific return opportunity near Hawaii.

These checkpoints gave SpaceX opportunities to end the mission safely over open water rather than commit an unhealthy spacecraft to the return across land.

The final check also revealed something particularly interesting about how SpaceX manages the recovery.

During the webcast, Kate Tice reported that every team had given the go-ahead, including Stage 2, the heat shield, flaps, structures, aerodynamics, guidance, navigation and control, and even the launch tower itself.

Yes, the tower was literally part of the go/no-go poll!

But passing those checks didn't eliminate the risks of the return.

Lars Blackmore explained that once Starship began flying over land, ground operators faced roughly 21 minutes during which they couldn't intervene.

For that entire stretch, the spacecraft had to rely on its onboard autonomous systems to follow the planned route and manage its descent.

That's an enormous responsibility for the flight-control software, especially with an orbital spacecraft crossing land and maneuvering around populated areas.

And the contingency planning didn't end with those 21 minutes.

Once Starship's return trajectory brought it back offshore over the Gulf, the flight plan still provided a final opportunity to divert the vehicle into the water if a safe tower catch was no longer possible.

That last detail says a lot.

Even after surviving orbital reentry, crossing thousands of kilometers, and arriving right off Starbase, Ship 42 could still have been diverted into the Gulf because of a problem with the launch tower.

In effect, SpaceX has made the tower part of the spacecraft's recovery system, with its own readiness affecting whether the mission can end with a successful catch.

A spacecraft can complete an entire orbital mission and return safely through the atmosphere, yet still have to abandon its catch because something on the ground isn't ready.

SpaceX designed its recovery system to account for that exact possibility. And making both the ship and its launch tower dependable enough to repeat these operations will be essential to achieving rapid reusability.

Comparing South Baldwin High Schools

The Alabama Department of Education’s state report card data provides a detailed side-by-side comparison of public high schools across accountability metrics, academic achievement, graduation rates, and student demographics. An analysis of the three local secondary campuses—Orange Beach Middle/High School, Gulf Shores High School, and Foley High School—highlights key differences in performance and school profiles across the region.

It should be noted that Orange Beach operates as a combined middle and high school, serving students in grades 7 through 12 under a single administrative campus structure. Unlike traditional standalone high schools that strictly encapsulate grades 9 through 12, Orange Beach’s report card metrics, total enrollment figures, and academic growth data represent the performance of both middle and high school student bodies combined.

Overall State Report Card Scores & GrowthState accountability letter grades evaluate high schools based on academic indicators, student growth, graduation rates, and school environment metrics:

📷
Orange Beach Middle & High School (Orange Beach City Schools): 95, up from 94 and 85 in previous years.Academic Achievement Score: 83.92
Academic Growth Score: 100.00
Chronic Absenteeism Rate: Reduced from 27% down to under 12%

Gulf Shores High School (Gulf Shores City Schools): 93, up from 91 and 90 in previous years.Academic Achievement Score: 65.14
Academic Growth Score: 100.00
Chronic Absenteeism Rate: 12.72%

Foley High School (Baldwin County Public Schools): 80, up from 75 in previous years.Statewide overall testing rank places in the bottom 50% statewide.

Graduation Rates & College/Career ReadinessSecondary outcomes across all three campuses show distinct differences in graduation completion rates and post-secondary preparation:
Orange Beach Middle & High School:Graduation Rate: Earned 100% of possible accountability points for graduation rate, achieving a 100% state-recognized graduation rate (99% federal).
College & Career Readiness (CCR): 100% credentialing rate.
Advanced Placement (AP): Elevated to Silver AP standing with 191 students completing 519 AP exams and a 64% qualifying score rate (3 or higher).

Gulf Shores High School:Graduation Rate: 100% average graduation rate.
Advanced Placement (AP): Offers 14 AP courses with an AP exam pass rate of ~38% and high enrollment in AP Math and Science.

Foley High School:Graduation Rate: 77% graduation rate, below the Alabama state average of 88%.

Academic Assessment & Subject ProficiencyStandardized assessment metrics reflect student proficiency levels across core subject areas:
Orange Beach Middle & High School:Reading/ELA Proficiency: 67%
Math Proficiency: 58%
Average ACT composite score: 20.6 (rising to 24–25 average among tested cohorts).

Gulf Shores High School:Reading/ELA Proficiency: 54%
Math Proficiency: 42%
Average ACT composite score: 25.

Foley High School:Math Proficiency: 30%
Reading Proficiency: 21%
Science Proficiency: 30%.

Campus Enrollment & Demographic ContextThe three high schools vary significantly in overall student population size and community demographics:
Orange Beach Middle & High School:Total Enrollment: ~647–650 students (Grades 7–12)
School Type: Small-town municipal city school system established in 2022.

Gulf Shores High School:Total Enrollment: ~749 students (Grades 9–12)
Student-to-Teacher Ratio: 15:1.

Foley High School:Total Enrollment: ~1,520–1,634 students (Grades 9–12)
Demographic Profile: High diversity body with minority enrollment at 58%–59% and 68% eligible for free or reduced lunch.

Taken as a whole, the performance and trajectory of these secondary campuses underscore a deep, community-wide dedication to public education across South Baldwin County. Whether through the creation of focused municipal school districts in Orange Beach and Gulf Shores aimed at targeted local investment, or the sustained academic growth initiatives within Baldwin County Public Schools at Foley High School, the region continuously prioritizes student achievement and post-secondary readiness. As enrollment expands alongside the area’s growth, South Baldwin’s high schools demonstrate a shared commitment to elevating academic standards, broadening career pathways, and supporting student success at every level.

It doesn't matter. The RINO's in the @GOP don't give one $hit. Let the FKN democrats trample them into the ground. Bunch of weak kneed morons that couldn't care less about the voters. @SenateGOP 

The November 2026 midterms did not deliver clean results. They delivered a cascade of red flags that any honest observer must confront. This left many Americans questioning whether the results truly reflected the will of the voters. Federal data, documented cases, Election Day failures, mail-in anomalies, and viral evidence of irregularities form a pattern that cannot be dismissed as isolated human error. Federal agencies themselves documented the scale of the problem. The Department of Homeland Security reported more than 1,600 active voter fraud investigations, over 150 arrests, and roughly 300,000 suspicious records under review in the run-up to the election. A million-dollar reward was offered for tips. These are not the statistics of a secure system. They are the statistics of a system under siege.

The Heritage Foundation’s database of proven election fraud cases – more than 1,500 documented instances and over 1,300 criminal convictions – shows this is not a new phenomenon. It is a long-standing vulnerability that federal authorities were still racing to contain as voters went to the polls. When hundreds of thousands of records are flagged through cross-checks of voter rolls, immigration data, and state files, the claim that “nothing is happening” collapses. An automated flag is not yet a conviction, but 1,620 formal inquiries nationwide is not clerical noise. It is a warning.

Election Day itself exposed the machinery’s fragility at the worst possible moments. In Westchester County, New York, during the razor-thin congressional race between Mike Lawler and Cait Conley, optical scanners suddenly stopped accepting Election Day ballots. Republicans vote heavily on Election Day. The machines failed precisely when those ballots were being cast. Officials blamed a programming update that created a formatting mismatch with the printed ballots. Voters were told to drop their paper into emergency compartments. The optics were disastrous: in a competitive district, the very systems designed to count votes rejected the votes of one side’s strongest turnout method. Similar failures and “glitches” appeared elsewhere. Videos from multiple states captured touchscreens flipping candidate selections when voters tapped them. Capacitive screens can lose calibration. Knuckles can brush edges. But the pattern of these failures occurring in high-stakes races is what demands explanation, not dismissal.

The software behind these machines compounds the distrust. Companies such as Liberty Vote – formerly Dominion – run proprietary code that the public cannot inspect. Rumors of vendor influence, remote access capabilities, and past controversies refuse to die. Officials insist the machines are air-gapped and subjected to Logic and Accuracy tests. They insist post-election audits of paper batches provide the final check. Yet when the same systems produce sudden rejections and screen flips at critical moments, confidence evaporates. Software can be tested. It can also be compromised. The public is asked to trust black-box systems whose vendors have faced years of suspicion.

Mail-in voting supplied the most dramatic shifts. Across California and multiple swing states, candidates who led on Election Night watched their leads disappear as batch after batch of mail-in ballots arrived over subsequent days and nights. The so-called “blue shift” is presented as a natural result of processing rules that delay the opening and scanning of mail ballots. Signature verification takes time. Flattening and review take time. But the consistent directional effect – late ballots moving races in one direction – creates the appearance of a system that can be gamed by volume and timing. Viral video from Ventura County showed mail-in envelopes punched with two holes. Critics correctly noted that those holes could allow workers to see how ballots were marked and selectively discard them. Officials offered explanations about tactile orientation for the visually impaired and empty-envelope checks. The public saw a process that invited abuse.

Concentrated registrations at commercial mail facilities have long been a red flag for fraud investigators. Ballot harvesting – paid operatives collecting stacks of mail ballots from nursing homes, apartment complexes, and other high-density locations – remains legal in too many jurisdictions. Unique barcodes and signature matching are cited as safeguards. Those safeguards still leave room for pressure, coercion, and selective delivery of harvested ballots into drop boxes.

Online platforms and comment sections filled with firsthand accounts from poll watchers, statistical charts showing suspiciously uniform shift bands, and reports of major seizures, including claims of an FBI raid on a Houston warehouse containing 20,000 fake ballots. Courts demand physical evidence under oath and reject volume of online reports as insufficient. That legal standard protects against frivolous challenges. It also leaves unresolved the widespread perception – fueled by federal investigation numbers, machine failures timed to Election Day voting, late-night ballot dumps, and registration anomalies – that the system failed to deliver transparent, trustworthy results.

Administrative friction is real. Printers jam. Programming updates fail. Mail processing stretches for days. Those are not imaginary problems. They are the exact points of vulnerability that allow errors – or worse – to affect outcomes. When the same friction repeatedly disadvantages one side’s preferred voting method, when federal agencies are investigating thousands of cases while offering cash rewards for tips, and when the public watches leads evaporate under late mail-in batches, the conclusion is unavoidable: the 2026 midterms were compromised. The safeguards that exist on paper did not prevent the patterns that now define the election. Americans who demand cleaner elections are not conspiracy theorists. They are citizens who can add.

November 16 has assembled a collection of events so thoroughly deranged that even a seasoned storyteller might ask for a rewrite—or simply close the book and go lie down.

A conqueror invites an emperor to a meeting that immediately turns into a catastrophe, then learns the captive ruler is willing to empty a room of treasure for the chance to walk away, as if the entire episode were some sort of expensive misunderstanding. A novelist receives a death sentence, faces a firing squad, and is spared at the very last moment—an experience that qualifies as research only if one has an unusually flexible definition of the term. A radio telescope sends a carefully encoded message toward the stars, essentially mailing a postcard to a destination where the delivery time makes ordinary impatience look almost reasonable.

Elsewhere, a man goes looking for a lost hammer and instead finds an ancient fortune buried in a European field, because the universe apparently prefers punchlines to logic. And just when the day seems to have exhausted its supply of improbable developments, a beloved snack cake becomes the focus of a nationwide buying frenzy, as if the continued existence of cream-filled sponge were suddenly a matter of public order.

Five strange events, one remarkable novelist, and a date that clearly refuses to behave itself.

Cue the chaos. Let's roll. 💥

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

❓ HISTORY QUIZ OF THE DAY

On November 16, 1992, Eric Lawes was searching a field in Suffolk, England, for something his friend had misplaced.

What did he discover instead?

[A] A buried Viking ship.

[B] A medieval royal crown.

[C] A vast hoard of Roman treasure.

[D] A forgotten military bunker.

👇 (Answer at the end of the issue.)

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

⭐️ MAIN EVENTS

👑 1532 — THE EMPEROR, THE CONQUISTADOR & THE ROOMFUL OF GOLD

November 16, 1532 | Cajamarca, Inca Empire (present-day Peru)

Francisco Pizarro had fewer than 200 Spanish soldiers. In front of him stood the ruler of the Inca Empire, Atahualpa, accompanied by thousands of followers.

The odds seemed absurdly unequal—but Pizarro had no intention of fighting a conventional battle.

Atahualpa had recently emerged victorious from a civil war against his half-brother Huáscar. Pizarro, who had arrived in the region with Spanish authorization to explore and conquer, recognized the political divisions that had weakened the empire. He invited Atahualpa to meet him at Cajamarca, presenting the encounter as a diplomatic gathering.

On the evening of November 16, Atahualpa entered the town's square in a magnificent litter, accompanied by a large, largely unarmed entourage. Pizarro's men were concealed in buildings around the plaza. A Spanish friar, Vicente de Valverde, approached the emperor and demanded that he accept Christianity and the authority of the Spanish Crown.

Atahualpa refused.

The Spanish then launched a sudden attack. Gunfire, cavalry, and steel weapons turned the crowded square into a massacre. Atahualpa was seized, and the capture of the emperor gave Pizarro extraordinary leverage over the empire.

The captive ruler soon realized what interested his captors most: gold. He offered to fill a room with gold and two rooms with silver in exchange for his freedom. The ransom was collected, but the treasure did not save him. Pizarro's forces eventually executed Atahualpa in 1533.

The capture at Cajamarca became a decisive turning point in the Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire.

🧩 TRIVIA: Pizarro's force was astonishingly small compared with the thousands accompanying Atahualpa. The Spanish advantage came not simply from weapons and horses, but from surprise, the confined setting, and the political divisions already weakening the Inca state.

🏴‍☠️ HUBRIS: Atahualpa entered the meeting as the most powerful ruler in the region. Within hours, he was a prisoner bargaining for his life—and the men holding him had discovered that an emperor could be turned into a ransom account.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Power can be immense and still be vulnerable when an enemy understands where it is concentrated.

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

⚖️ 1849 — DOSTOEVSKY’S DATE WITH THE FIRING SQUAD

November 16, 1849 | St. Petersburg, Russian Empire

Fyodor Dostoevsky was a young writer whose literary career was just beginning when his involvement with a group of politically outspoken intellectuals brought him into conflict with the Russian authorities.
The group, known as the Petrashevsky Circle, met to discuss literature, philosophy, and social reform. In the repressive political climate of Tsar Nicholas I's Russia, such conversations could be treated as a threat to the state.

Dostoevsky was arrested in April 1849. After months of imprisonment and interrogation, he was sentenced to death on November 16.

The sentence was not carried out immediately. On December 22, Dostoevsky and other condemned prisoners were taken to Semyonovsky Square. They were dressed for execution, and the preparations for a firing squad began. Some prisoners were already tied to posts when a messenger arrived with news that the Tsar had commuted their sentences.

The reprieve had been arranged in advance. The prisoners, however, had not been told. They were made to experience the apparent certainty of imminent death before learning that they would live.

Dostoevsky's sentence was replaced with four years of hard labor in Siberia, followed by compulsory military service. The ordeal profoundly affected him. His later writing would explore guilt, suffering, faith, freedom, and the darkest corners of the human mind with an intensity few novelists have matched.

🧩 TRIVIA: Dostoevsky later described the staged execution as an experience that made him acutely conscious of the value of every remaining minute. In a letter to his brother, written on the day of the execution ceremony, he reflected on how precious life seemed when he believed he had almost none left.

🕵️ MYSTERY: The reprieve was not a last-second act of mercy. The decision had already been made, but the prisoners were deliberately kept unaware until the execution ceremony was underway. The reason for subjecting them to that psychological ordeal remains a disturbing feature of the episode.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A reprieve can save a life. It cannot necessarily erase what a person has been made to endure.

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

📡 1974 — EARTH SENDS A MESSAGE TO THE STARS

November 16, 1974 | Arecibo Observatory, Puerto Rico

Humanity has spent a long time wondering whether anyone else is out there. On this day, scientists decided to send a message.

From the enormous radio telescope at Arecibo, Puerto Rico, researchers transmitted a carefully constructed sequence of radio pulses toward the globular star cluster Messier 13, approximately 25,000 light-years away.
The message contained 1,679 binary digits. When arranged in the correct pattern, they formed a graphic representation of basic information about Earth and its inhabitants: numbers, important chemical elements, components of DNA, the DNA double helix, a human figure, the solar system, and the Arecibo telescope itself.

The project was associated with astronomers Frank Drake and Carl Sagan, among other scientists. It was transmitted during a ceremony marking a major upgrade to the observatory.

The message was not an expectation of an imminent reply. Even if an intelligent civilization in M13 received it immediately and responded without delay, the round trip would take roughly 50,000 years.

🧩 TRIVIA: The 1,679 bits can be arranged into a rectangle measuring 23 by 73. Both numbers are prime, a mathematical choice intended to help a hypothetical recipient recognize the correct arrangement of the message.

🔮 PROLEPTIC: The message attempted to communicate with an intelligence that might have no shared language, history, or culture with humanity. Its designers relied on mathematics, chemistry, and biology as possible common ground—an introduction built for a conversation that might not begin for millennia.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Sometimes the most extraordinary message is not the one that gets an answer, but the one that proves we were willing to ask the question.

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🏺 1992 — THE LOST HAMMER AND BRITAIN’S ROMAN FORTUNE

November 16, 1992 | Hoxne, Suffolk, England

Eric Lawes went into a field near the village of Hoxne with a metal detector. He was looking for a hammer that his friend, tenant farmer Peter Whatling, had lost.

He found something considerably more valuable.

The detector signaled underground, and Lawes began uncovering Roman coins and precious objects. Rather than dig everything out himself, he stopped and reported the discovery. The following day, archaeologists from the Suffolk Archaeological Unit, directed by Judith Plouviez, carried out a controlled excavation of the remaining deposit.

The find became known as the Hoxne Hoard, the richest treasure discovery from Roman Britain. The recovered collection contained 14,865 coins, along with approximately 200 pieces of jewelry and silver tableware. It included gold bracelets, necklaces, a remarkable body chain, silver spoons, ladles, and ornate pepper pots.

And the hammer? It had brought Lawes to the field in the first place. The treasure was the unexpected bonus.

🧩 TRIVIA: One of the silver pepper pots takes the form of a richly dressed woman. A rotating disc in its base could be turned to close the container, open larger holes for filling it, or reveal tiny holes for sprinkling pepper. Even Roman luxury dining came with adjustable settings.

🐶 SPOT: Lawes' decision to stop digging and report the find was crucial. The controlled excavation the next day allowed archaeologists to recover the remaining objects while preserving valuable information about how the hoard had been buried.

🌀 OBSCURE: A gold bracelet from the hoard carries the inscription “UTERE FELIX DOMINA IULIANE,” meaning roughly, “Use this happily, Lady Juliane.” The message suggests a personal gift to a woman named Juliane, but her identity—and the identity of the person who gave her the bracelet—remain unknown.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A lost hammer led to a buried fortune. But the real value of the discovery came from recognizing that the objects were more than treasure: they were evidence.

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🧁 2012 — THE GREAT TWINKIE PANIC

November 16, 2012 | United States

For generations, Twinkies had been a familiar fixture of American lunchboxes, convenience stores, and late-night snack cravings. Then, on November 16, 2012, their future suddenly looked uncertain.

Hostess Brands announced that it was winding down operations after a nationwide labor strike crippled production and distribution. The company said it would seek permission from bankruptcy court to close its business and sell its assets. Approximately 18,500 jobs were at stake.

The announcement triggered a remarkable consumer reaction. Customers rushed to stores to buy Twinkies and other Hostess products before supplies disappeared. Some shelves emptied quickly. People bought boxes by the armful, while online sellers began offering the familiar snack cakes at wildly inflated prices.

The answer, eventually, was yes. Hostess brands and assets were acquired, and Twinkies returned to store shelves in 2013.

The panic had been real. The disappearance was temporary.

🧩 TRIVIA: Hostess said the shutdown put approximately 18,500 employees at risk. The company’s announcement also covered a long list of familiar brands, including Ding Dongs, Ho Hos, Sno Balls, Donettes, and Wonder Bread.

⚠️ IRONY: A company facing a major labor dispute and financial collapse became the subject of a consumer frenzy focused largely on snack cakes. The threatened loss of thousands of jobs was serious; the public's most visible reaction was a race to stock up on Twinkies.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Scarcity can transform an everyday product into an object of sudden obsession. Sometimes the panic begins before the shelves are even empty.

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

🎙️ HARVEY’S CORNER

📚 CHINUA ACHEBE — THE MAN WHO GAVE A NATION BACK ITS VOICE

Good day, everybody.

Imagine growing up in a place where the stories told about your people were written largely by people who had never lived among them. Your history was described through someone else's eyes. Your traditions were misunderstood, your culture reduced to stereotypes, and your people too often appeared as supporting characters in a story about somebody else's greatness.

Now imagine deciding to do something about it.

That was part of the journey of Chinua Achebe, born November 16, 1930, in Ogidi, in southeastern Nigeria.

Achebe grew up in an Igbo household where traditional beliefs and customs existed alongside the Christian faith embraced by his parents. He was exposed to both worlds from an early age. That experience gave him an unusual perspective: he could understand the attractions and contradictions of each without pretending that either was simple.

He was an exceptionally thoughtful young man, drawn to books, language, and the power of stories. He attended University College, Ibadan, where his studies and growing interest in African history and literature helped shape the direction of his life. After graduating, he joined the Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation.

But Achebe had something larger in mind than a career in broadcasting.

He wanted to write about Africa from the inside.

In 1958, he published a novel that would become one of the most influential works in modern African literature: Things Fall Apart.

Its central character, Okonkwo, is a respected and fiercely determined man in an Igbo community. He has built his life around strength, reputation, and the traditions of his society. But the arrival of Christian missionaries and British colonial authority begins to transform the world he knows. The resulting conflict is not simply between Africans and Europeans. It unfolds within families, friendships, religious beliefs, and the community itself.

Achebe did something remarkable. He allowed readers to see this society before colonial rule through the lives of the people who inhabited it. They had laws, ceremonies, arguments, ambitions, humor, wisdom, rivalries, and deeply held beliefs. They were not waiting for Europeans to arrive and give their lives meaning.

That may sound obvious today. It was not how much of the English-language literary world had portrayed Africa.

Achebe did not write a simplistic defense of his culture, either. He showed its strengths and its flaws. Okonkwo himself is a complicated, sometimes destructive man. The novel's power comes from its refusal to turn human beings into convenient symbols.

Things Fall Apart became an international success, was translated into dozens of languages, and eventually became one of the most widely read African novels in the world. It helped change the way generations of readers understood African history and literature.

But Achebe's commitment to telling African stories did not end with fiction.

In 1962, he became the founding editor of Heinemann's African Writers Series, helping bring the work of other African authors to readers around the world. He understood that one voice, however influential, could never represent an entire continent. Other writers needed the opportunity to tell their own stories, too.

Then history placed his convictions under a different kind of pressure.

In 1967, Nigeria descended into civil war after the southeastern region declared itself the independent Republic of Biafra. Achebe supported Biafra and served as a diplomatic representative, traveling abroad to draw attention to the conflict and the humanitarian crisis.

He was no longer simply writing about the consequences of political decisions. He was living through them.

The war ended in 1970 with Biafra's defeat. The suffering, displacement, and loss left a lasting mark on Achebe. His later essays and political writing reflected his belief that writers could not always remain comfortably detached from the societies in which they lived.

Then, in 1990, another devastating event changed his life.

While traveling in Nigeria, Achebe was involved in a serious automobile accident that left him paralyzed from the waist down. He was flown to England for medical treatment and later continued his academic career in the United States.

For a man whose life had been devoted to writing, teaching, and public engagement, the physical consequences were enormous. Yet he continued to work, publish, teach, and speak. He held academic positions at Bard College and Brown University, influencing students and readers far beyond Nigeria.

His books continued to reach new generations. Among his other important works were No Longer at Ease, Arrow of God, A Man of the People, and Anthills of the Savannah.

Achebe died in Boston on March 21, 2013, at the age of eighty-two.

But consider what remained.

A boy from Ogidi had grown up to challenge the way an entire literary tradition portrayed his continent. A novelist had opened doors for countless other writers. A public intellectual had insisted that literature could not be separated entirely from questions of power, identity, and responsibility.

Achebe did not give Africa a voice. Africa had always had voices. What he did was help make the world listen—and make it harder for the world to pretend it had never heard them.

And now, you know the rest of the story.

────────────── ❧ ────────────────

⚖️ CLOSING

Look at the lives behind today's stories. Atahualpa tried to buy his freedom with a fortune in gold, only to discover that his captors wanted the treasure more than they wanted to honor their bargain. Dostoevsky was forced to face his own execution before being granted a reprieve. The scientists at Arecibo sent a message into a universe that might never answer. Eric Lawes found a fortune while searching for a lost hammer. And Chinua Achebe spent his life challenging the world's assumptions about Africa and the people who called it home.

Their stories remind us that history is shaped by more than kings and conquerors. It is shaped by people who endure, discover, question, create, and sometimes change the way generations after them see the world.

Pizarro's conquest, Dostoevsky's survival, Lawes's discovery, and Achebe's literary legacy all left marks that outlasted the moments themselves. Even that message from Arecibo continues its journey into the unknown.

And then there were the Twinkies. Some legacies are simply harder to explain than others. 🤭
