Fluted Wall Paneling vs Comb-Profile Siding: Which Texture Wins for Modern Designs by US Lumber Brokers https://t.co/cxwk4IaNAp 

The Architect’s Challenge: Achieving Expressive Texture Without Compromising Performance
Modern architecture demands material honesty. You’re designing homes that celebrate natural wood, not hide it behind flat facades. Yet selecting between textured profiles means navigating competing demands: visual richness, structural integrity, weather exposure, and long-term maintenance.

Architects working in the contemporary space know the tension well. A design that relies on expressive wood textures to create warmth and visual interest must also withstand Texas weather-intense sun, humidity swings, and occasional freeze-thaw cycles. Choosing the wrong profile compromises either aesthetics or durability. Choosing poorly sourced material undermines both.

We understand this challenge because we work with firms like Lake|Flato and Page every project. These practices treat wood texture as a design language, not an afterthought. That means your supplier must deliver consistent, high-quality material in the exact profile your design demands, backed by real performance data and sourcing transparency.
The right material choice elevates a home from nice to distinctive. Poor material choice creates callbacks, warranty disputes, and damaged client relationships.

What Sets Fluted Wall Paneling and Comb-Profile Siding Apart

Fluted wall paneling features parallel, evenly-spaced grooves running vertically across the board face. These grooves create shadow lines that deepen with angle and light, generating visual texture without raised edges. The profile sits flat to the substrate, making it a natural choice for accent walls, interior-exterior transitions, and areas where you want dramatic effect without structural complication.
Comb-profile siding uses alternating raised ridges and grooves-like a comb’s teeth. This profile delivers more aggressive shadow play and pronounced tactile texture. The raised portions create genuine three-dimensionality, which can catch water and debris more readily but also provides superior visual drama at distance.

The practical difference matters: fluted paneling sits proud of the substrate by minimal amounts, simplifying flashing and trim. Comb-profile siding’s raised ridges require more thoughtful flashing details, especially at penetrations and transitions. Neither approach is wrong; the choice depends on your design intent and site conditions.

We stock both profiles in the same premium species-clear and vertical grain Western Red Cedar, hemlock, Douglas fir, and cypress-so your selection reflects pure design preference, not material availability.

Material Quality and Species Selection: Where Our Inventory Leads

Species choice determines how texture reads in real light. Fluted patterns in tight-grain Douglas fir or hemlock emphasize linearity; the same profile in wide-grain Southern Yellow Pine creates visual complexity as growth rings interact with the grooves.
Clear and vertical grain cedar brings warmth and tonal consistency that lets texture dominate the visual story. We prioritize vertical grain specifically because it minimizes movement and cupping-critical for fluted or comb profiles where profile integrity directly affects shadow quality. Horizontal grain cedar tends to distort over time, softening the designed texture into an uncontrolled appearance.

Hemlock offers similar stability with cooler undertones. Douglas fir delivers durability plus the visual pop that contemporary designs often demand. Cypress provides unmatched rot resistance in areas exposed to ground contact or constant moisture.

For projects requiring maximum durability without traditional softwood grain patterns, our inventory includes thermally modified ash, pine, and poplar-materials engineered to resist cupping and movement while accepting fluted or comb profiles that maintain crisp lines across decades.

We also stock hardwood alternatives: Ipe, Cumaru, Garapa, and Massaranduba. These deliver dimensional stability and natural resistance that eliminates finish concerns, though their density requires precision milling to achieve true fluted clarity. Tigerwood bridges the gap-harder than traditional softwoods yet machinable enough for detailed profiles.

Your species selection should reflect exposure, maintenance philosophy, and the specific visual character your design demands. We help you match intention to material.

Durability and Weather Resistance: A Head-to-Head Comparison

Fluted paneling’s minimal profile variance means water drains predictably. Grooves funnel moisture downward without pooling in ridges. This translates to simpler finishing strategies and lower maintenance burden. Paint or stain adheres more uniformly because you’re coating flat surfaces plus vertical wall areas, not complex three-dimensional geometry.
Comb-profile siding’s raised ridges create horizontal ledges where moisture can collect momentarily before draining. Quality installation with proper flashing mitigates this risk, but the profile demands more rigorous detailing at roof lines, window heads, and horizontal transitions. The tradeoff: comb profiles handle freeze-thaw cycles well because the raised ridges allow expansion and contraction without buckling the overall plane.

Both profiles perform well in Texas climate when specified correctly. Cypress and cedar naturally resist moisture damage. Douglas fir and hemlock require proper finish systems-we recommend exterior-grade primers and two-coat paint systems for maximum durability. Thermally modified materials eliminate finish concerns almost entirely; the thermal treatment changes wood structure at the cellular level, essentially rendering the material rot and cupping resistant without surface coatings.

WUI (Wildland Urban Interface) Class A fire-rated options exist for both profiles if your project sits in high-risk areas around Austin Hill Country or similar zones. These materials meet stringent fire ratings without sacrificing the texture-rich aesthetic your design requires.

Aesthetic Impact and Design Flexibility: Creating Distinctive Exteriors

Fluted paneling works brilliantly for continuous wall expression, feature walls, and large uninterrupted surfaces. The repeating groove pattern reads as intentional rhythm from distance; up close, it invites tactile engagement. Contemporary homes often leverage fluted walls to create visual lightness-the parallel lines recede, making substantial walls feel less massive.
Comb-profile siding delivers presence. It reads aggressively from twenty feet away, making modest elevations feel architecturally significant. This profile suits accent applications, feature areas, and homes where you want wood to dominate the visual narrative.

The interplay between profile and lighting is crucial. South and west-facing fluted walls in morning light read completely different from east or north exposures. Comb profiles amplify this variation-morning and evening light creates shadow patterns that shift across the elevation. We’ve worked with architects who deliberately specify comb profiles on specific elevations precisely because the light-responsive texture reinforces the home’s connection to its site and time of day.
Color and grain consistency interact with profile selection too. Wide-variation stain palettes pair well with comb profiles (the ridges absorb color variation naturally). High-clarity natural finishes or paint colors demand vertical grain material and tight milling tolerances, where fluted profiles maximize the payoff.

Sustainability and FSC Certification: Our Commitment to Responsible Sourcing

Contemporary architecture demands material integrity at every level-including sourcing. We supply FSC certified wood products across our full inventory: clear and vertical grain cedar, hemlock, Douglas fir, cypress, and all hardwood species.

FSC certification ensures responsible forest management, fair labor practices, and community benefit. For architects seeking LEED credits or simply designing with material honesty, FSC verification matters. We maintain full chain-of-custody documentation; you receive our certified material with sourcing transparency your clients deserve.
Thermally modified products add another sustainability dimension: these materials extend wood life through thermal treatment rather than chemical processing, reducing finish maintenance across the home’s lifespan. Less maintenance means fewer surface coatings, which benefits both durability and environmental impact.

Composite alternatives-TimberTech, Trex, and Fiberon products-eliminate wood entirely while delivering texture analogous to fluted or comb profiles. These materials suit architects prioritizing zero maintenance and maximum longevity, though they carry different environmental considerations than solid wood. We stock leading brands so your specification reflects authentic design choice, not material limitation.

Installation Considerations and Long-Term Maintenance Requirements

Fluted paneling installation is straightforward: boards attach to standard framing with fastener placement between grooves (fasteners remain hidden). Flashing at transitions requires attention but follows conventional practices. The profile’s simplicity means installers making their first fluted installation still achieve professional results.

Comb-profile siding demands more precision. The raised ridges create potential water intrusion points at fastener holes; quality installation uses stainless steel fasteners and sealant protocols. Flashing complexity increases at roof lines and penetrations because the profile’s three-dimensionality requires customized trim details. Working with installers experienced in textured profiles prevents costly callbacks.
Both profiles benefit from annual inspection: debris accumulation in fluted grooves typically clears with rain, but roof gutters and eaves demand seasonal cleaning. Comb profiles require slightly more attention at horizontal transitions where wind-driven rain might find purchase in ridge-and-valley geometry.

Finish maintenance depends on material selection. Solid wood requires recoating every 5–7 years for painted finishes, longer for stain. Thermally modified materials extend this interval to 10+ years. Hardwoods like Ipe demand minimal maintenance but require professional refinishing if color change occurs. Composite materials require virtually no maintenance beyond occasional cleaning.

We provide detailed maintenance guides for every species and profile combination we supply. Your specification should include these requirements in project documentation so clients understand the material’s care needs upfront.

Why US Lumber Brokers Is Your Definitive Partner for Texture-Rich Designs

You’re designing homes that demand more than standard lumber suppliers provide. We’ve built our business specifically to serve architects and builders pursuing contemporary wood-forward design. Our inventory depth-clear and vertical grain softwoods, premium hardwoods, thermally modified products, fire-rated materials, and leading composite brands-means your specification encounters zero availability friction.

Beyond inventory, we understand the distinction between fluted and comb profiles as design language, not commodity products. We stock both in multiple species, mill custom profiles on request, and provide sourcing transparency through FSC certification and chain-of-custody documentation. When you specify US Lumber Brokers, your material arrives exactly as designed-consistent, high-quality, and backed by suppliers who understand architectural intent.
Our Texas roots matter too. We work with the same architects and builders across Austin, Dallas, Houston, and Hill Country. We know the climate challenges these projects face. We understand the site-specific variations that influence species and profile selection. When you need material advice that reflects genuine regional expertise, not generic industry recommendations, we provide that grounded perspective.

Start your next project with a material consultation. Bring your design intent, site exposure, and maintenance philosophy. We’ll recommend the exact profile, species, and sourcing approach that transforms your textured wood vision into a home that performs beautifully for decades.

US Lumber Brokers

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

What’s the practical difference between fluted wall paneling and comb-profile siding for our Texas climate?

We find that fluted paneling offers deeper, more dramatic shadow lines that photograph exceptionally well for contemporary designs, while comb-profile siding provides a subtler linear texture that weathers more evenly in our intense sun. Both profiles perform well in Texas heat, but fluted designs can trap slightly more moisture in the grooves, so we always recommend specifying species with natural rot resistance like Western Red Cedar or Cypress for those applications. The choice really depends on whether your design calls for bold architectural expression or refined understatement.
Do we stock fluted and comb-profile options in the wood species architects typically specify?
We maintain inventory in vertical grain Western Red Cedar, Douglas Fir, and Hemlock in both profiles, and we can source additional species like Cypress and thermally modified options through our manufacturing relationships. Since we manufacture some of our own products, we also work with architects to create custom profile specifications when a project demands something beyond our standard offerings. Our FSC-certified inventory ensures you’re specifying responsibly sourced material regardless of profile.

Which textured profile requires less maintenance in the long run?
Comb-profile siding generally demands fewer maintenance visits because its shallower grooves shed debris more easily and dry faster after rain, making it ideal for clients who prefer a low-touch approach. Fluted paneling creates that striking architectural impact, but the deeper channels benefit from more frequent cleaning and inspection to prevent moisture accumulation, particularly in shaded exposures. We recommend discussing maintenance expectations with your builders early, as this often influences which profile makes the most sense for specific project locations.

FREE SPORTS PICKS - MONDAY, NOVEMBER 16, 2026

MONDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL, NBA, COLLEGE BASKETBALL AND NHL FREE PICKS!

Monday’s PicksDepot betting card features 20 free selections from professional sports handicappers. The headliner is Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, where handicappers are divided on both the point spread and the total.

Today’s NBA selections include Chicago-Cleveland, Memphis-Washington and Houston-Miami. College basketball offers three early-season opportunities, while the NHL card features Montreal-New York and Vancouver-Utah.

Every selection is credited to the individual handicapper who released it, with the published line, betting analysis and important matchup considerations. Several handicappers disagree on the same games, making line shopping particularly important. Prices can change before game time.

NFL FREE PICKS - MONDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL

LOS ANGELES CHARGERS AT BALTIMORE RAVENS - 8:15 PM ET

Baltimore’s quarterback situation dominates tonight’s matchup. Newly acquired Jacoby Brissett is expected to make his Ravens debut after the offense struggled badly without Lamar Jackson. Baltimore has scored 13 or fewer points in four consecutive games, but the Chargers have also struggled defensively, allowing 44 points to Houston in their previous contest.

Los Angeles counters with Justin Herbert, whose finger imaging reportedly came back negative. The Chargers have experienced serious pass-protection problems, however, and Herbert faces another difficult assignment against a Baltimore defense looking to recover its earlier form.

The free-pick board includes opposing selections on Baltimore -4.5 and Los Angeles +4.5 or +5, along with Over 38.5 and Unders at 39 and 39.5.

HUNTER PRICE - CHARGERS/RAVENS OVER 38.5 (-110)

Price backs a higher-scoring game despite both offenses experiencing recent difficulties. The total reflects Baltimore’s offensive collapse without Jackson, but the arrival of Brissett introduces a different quarterback profile and the possibility of more consistent passing production.

The Ravens still have Derrick Henry, Zay Flowers and Mark Andrews available as established offensive weapons. Meanwhile, the Chargers’ defense has allowed substantial production in recent games. This wager needs only 39 combined points, a relatively modest threshold if Brissett can stabilize Baltimore’s passing game and Herbert generates enough offense for Los Angeles.

DUSTIN HAWKINS - CHARGERS/RAVENS UNDER 39.5 (-115)

Hawkins takes the opposite approach, backing the Under at 39.5. Baltimore’s quarterback transition does not guarantee an immediate offensive improvement, especially against an opponent that can pressure the passer and force difficult third-down situations.

The Chargers’ offensive line has struggled to protect Herbert, while Baltimore’s offense has repeatedly failed to produce sustained scoring drives. If both teams emphasize field position, avoid unnecessary risks and settle for field goals rather than touchdowns, the scoring could remain below 40 points. The extra point compared with Under 38.5 provides meaningful protection.

BRODY VAUGHN - LOS ANGELES CHARGERS +4.5 (-108) AT BALTIMORE

Vaughn backs Los Angeles as a road underdog, getting more than a field goal against a Baltimore team still adjusting to its quarterback situation. The Ravens may benefit from Brissett’s experience, but installing a new starter creates uncertainty regarding offensive timing and execution.

Herbert gives the Chargers an established quarterback capable of keeping a game competitive, even when pass protection becomes a problem. The wager does not require Los Angeles to win outright. A Ravens victory by four points or fewer would still cash the Chargers +4.5.

MAX CHASE - LOS ANGELES CHARGERS +4.5 (-108) AT BALTIMORE

Chase joins Vaughn on Los Angeles at the same spread and price. Baltimore enters having lost four consecutive games, with its offensive struggles making it difficult to assume the Ravens can create substantial separation.

The Chargers’ defensive problems are a concern, particularly against Henry and Baltimore’s rushing attack, but the betting question is whether the Ravens deserve to be favored by more than four points while introducing a new quarterback.

Los Angeles needs to protect Herbert, avoid turnovers that create short fields and remain competitive into the fourth quarter. A one-possession game would give the underdog a realistic opportunity to cover.

COLE FAXON - CHARGERS/RAVENS UNDER 39.5 (-115)

Faxon also expects a relatively low-scoring Monday night game. Baltimore has averaged just 14.6 points across its previous five contests, according to the offensive numbers published with the matchup, and has failed to reach 14 points in four straight games.

Brissett’s arrival could improve the offense, but the Ravens still need to establish passing-game chemistry. On the other side, Herbert has absorbed considerable pressure behind a struggling offensive line.

Both teams have reasons to avoid unnecessary turnovers and protect field position. The Under 39.5 wins with 39 or fewer combined points and offers a better scoring threshold than Under 39.

BOBBY CONN - BALTIMORE RAVENS -4.5 (-110) VS. LOS ANGELES CHARGERS

Conn backs Baltimore to win by at least five points at home. The Ravens have struggled offensively, but replacing rookie Joe Fagnano with veteran Brissett could improve decision-making and give the offense a more dependable passing presence.

Baltimore still possesses dangerous skill-position personnel. Henry can force defenses to commit additional resources against the run, potentially creating opportunities for Flowers and Andrews.

The Chargers have allowed 27.4 points per game this season and are coming off a difficult defensive performance against Houston. Conn’s selection depends on Baltimore taking advantage of those weaknesses while preventing Herbert from keeping Los Angeles within one possession.

TIMOTHY BLACK - LOS ANGELES CHARGERS +5 (-110) AT BALTIMORE

Black backs Los Angeles with five points, obtaining a slightly larger cushion than the handicappers holding +4.5.

That half-point difference matters. A five-point Baltimore victory would push Chargers +5 but lose at +4.5. In a game with a relatively low total, every point becomes more valuable because fewer scoring possessions can make it difficult for either team to build a comfortable margin.

Herbert’s ability to generate scoring opportunities despite protection issues is critical. Baltimore’s recent offensive difficulties also strengthen the case that the Ravens could win without necessarily covering a spread of this size.

BLACK WIDOW - BALTIMORE RAVENS -4.5 (-110) VS. LOS ANGELES CHARGERS

Black Widow joins Conn on the Baltimore favorite, publishing the selection as a free Wiseguy play. The handicapper is taking the position that the Ravens’ home-field advantage, established offensive personnel and quarterback adjustment will be sufficient to overcome their recent struggles.

Baltimore’s defense also has an opportunity against a Chargers offensive line that has allowed substantial quarterback pressure. If the Ravens can disrupt Herbert and generate favorable field position, they could create the separation needed to cover.

The principal risk is another inefficient Baltimore offensive performance. Even a Ravens victory may not be enough if the game remains within four points.

STEVE JANUS - CHARGERS/RAVENS OVER 38.5 (-110)

Janus backs the Over at 38.5, joining Hunter Price on the same selection. The wager reflects the possibility that Baltimore’s recent offensive struggles have depressed the total beyond what the current matchup deserves.

Brissett is a veteran quarterback taking over an offense with established rushing and receiving options. Los Angeles also has the ability to generate offense through Herbert, even if its protection is inconsistent.

The Ravens have allowed substantial scoring during their recent losing streak, and the Chargers surrendered 44 points to Houston last week. Either defense creating turnovers or short fields could help push the combined score beyond 38.5.

JIMMY BOYD - CHARGERS/RAVENS OVER 38.5 (-110)

Boyd offers one of the more detailed arguments for the Over. He believes the market is placing too much emphasis on Baltimore’s recent offensive results, which were produced during a difficult period of quarterback instability.

Fagnano threw for only 60 yards against Jacksonville, averaging 3.3 yards per attempt with two interceptions. Brissett brings substantially more NFL starting experience and previously demonstrated the ability to move the football through the air.

Boyd also emphasizes the defenses. Baltimore has allowed approximately 28 points per game over its previous five contests, including 33 against Jacksonville, 36 against Buffalo and 35 against Cincinnati. Los Angeles is allowing 27.4 points per game this season.

Herbert’s finger imaging was encouraging, and the Chargers have multiple receiving options even with uncertainty surrounding Ladd McConkey. Boyd believes 38.5 is too low considering the defensive vulnerabilities and Baltimore’s quarterback upgrade.

ANDREW GOLD - CHARGERS/RAVENS UNDER 39 (-108)

Gold completes the group of Under selections, targeting a total of 39 at slightly better odds than the handicappers taking Under 39.5.

Baltimore’s recent offensive production raises reasonable questions about whether a quarterback change can immediately solve its problems. Los Angeles has also struggled to protect Herbert, and another game featuring heavy pressure could limit sustained drives.

The scoring threshold is important. Under 39 wins with 38 or fewer combined points and pushes at exactly 39. That makes it less attractive numerically than Under 39.5, although Gold’s -108 price is slightly better than the -115 attached to the higher number.

The matchup presents a genuine disagreement among PicksDepot handicappers: some expect Brissett to improve Baltimore’s offense immediately, while others believe quarterback transitions and pass-protection problems will keep scoring limited.

COLLEGE BASKETBALL FREE PICKS

BRIAN BITLER - RICHMOND +13.5 (-116) AT VIRGINIA TECH - 7:00 PM ET

Bitler backs Richmond with nearly 14 points against unbeaten Virginia Tech. The Hokies enter 4-0 and recently defeated Mount St. Mary’s 82-62, but Richmond has demonstrated considerable offensive potential during its 3-1 start.

The Spiders scored 100 points against UNC Asheville and 107 against Southern Virginia. Dominick Stewart has emerged as an important offensive contributor and scored 25 points in Richmond’s 80-70 loss to Southern Illinois.

Virginia Tech has the stronger defensive profile and can create additional opportunities through turnovers. The Hokies forced 23 turnovers against Mount St. Mary’s, which represents an important concern for Richmond.

However, Bitler believes the spread is excessive for an early-season nonconference game against a capable offensive opponent. Virginia Tech could control the contest and win by double digits without covering 13.5.

ROCKY ATKINSON - MINNESOTA -33.5 (-109) VS. WESTERN ILLINOIS - 8:00 PM ET

Atkinson backs Minnesota to produce a decisive home victory against Western Illinois. The Golden Gophers enter 4-0, while Western Illinois is 1-3.

Minnesota recently defeated Southern University 91-61, shooting 60% from the field and connecting on 13 three-pointers. Isaac Asuma contributed 23 points, while the Gophers dominated the rebounding battle 40-21.

Atkinson cites a historical system involving substantial home favorites with strong three-point shooting facing opponents with weak perimeter shooting. He reports the qualifying situation has produced a 52-22 record, covering 70.3%, since 1998.

The challenge is the enormous spread. Minnesota must win by at least 34 points, which requires consistent offensive execution and defensive intensity even if the result is no longer in doubt. Atkinson recommends a smaller play rather than treating the historical record as a guarantee.

MATT SULLIVAN - ABILENE CHRISTIAN/MISSOURI STATE OVER 141.5 (-110) - 8:00 PM ET

Sullivan backs the Over in Abilene Christian’s visit to Missouri State. The Bears enter 3-0 after scoring 88, 79 and 89 points in their first three games. However, all three victories came against Division II competition, making the offensive results difficult to project directly against a Division I opponent.

Abilene Christian enters 1-2 and recently lost 76-71 to Stephen F. Austin. The Wildcats have shown they can contribute offensively but have also experienced defensive problems, allowing 94 points against Colorado and 81 against Lamar.

Missouri State’s offensive size and interior opportunities could create favorable scoring chances, while Abilene Christian needs to contribute enough to make the Over attainable.

The selection needs 142 combined points. With such an early-season matchup, shooting efficiency, turnovers and pace will be particularly important in determining whether the teams can clear that number.

NBA FREE PICKS

BRANDON LEE - CHICAGO BULLS +9.5 (-102) AT CLEVELAND CAVALIERS - 7:10 PM ET

Lee backs Chicago with a substantial cushion against Cleveland. The Bulls have shown signs of improvement after a difficult stretch, recently defeating Atlanta 125-117 in overtime and Minnesota 117-106.

Cleveland has its own personnel questions. Evan Mobley is listed out with a toe injury, removing an important defensive presence and rebounder from the Cavaliers’ frontcourt. Donovan Mitchell, James Harden and Jarrett Allen could provide Cleveland with additional offensive strength after missing the previous game, making final availability important.

The Bulls’ argument rests on recent improvement and the significant point spread. Chicago does not need to win outright; a defeat by nine points or fewer would cash.

The published -102 price is also attractive compared with standard -110 odds, although Cleveland’s offensive ceiling remains a serious concern for anyone backing the underdog.

INFO PLAYS - WASHINGTON WIZARDS +5.5 (-110) VS. MEMPHIS GRIZZLIES - 7:10 PM ET

Info Plays backs Washington despite the Wizards entering on a seven-game losing streak. Memphis has been the stronger team, starting 9-4 overall and winning its first six road games.

Washington is coming off a 147-119 defeat against Houston in which the Rockets dominated the middle quarters and controlled the rebounding battle. Alex Sarr has been a productive contributor for the Wizards, but Washington needs better overall defensive execution to remain competitive.

Memphis has demonstrated consistent road performance, making the Grizzlies a difficult opponent to oppose. However, Info Plays receives 5.5 points with the home team, creating room for Washington to lose a relatively competitive contest and still cover.

The Wizards must improve their transition defense, avoid allowing Memphis easy second-chance points and keep the game close through the third quarter. The published number is particularly important because some broader-market prices have been shorter.

MIKE LUNDIN - HOUSTON ROCKETS/MIAMI HEAT UNDER 231 (-110) - 7:40 PM ET

Lundin believes the total has been inflated by recent scoring performances from both teams. Houston enters on a four-game winning streak, while Miami has recovered from an 0-4 start to win seven of its previous nine games, including four consecutive victories.

Houston just defeated Washington 147-119, with Amen Thompson scoring 26 points and Kevin Durant and Tari Eason adding 25 apiece. That extraordinary offensive performance could encourage bettors to expect another high-scoring contest.

Lundin instead emphasizes Houston’s defensive identity, rebounding and ability to disrupt opposing offensive possessions. He also believes Miami has experienced periods of inconsistent half-court scoring, even during its recent improvement.

The Rockets’ physicality and control of the glass could help reduce second-chance scoring opportunities for Miami. The Heat must also defend more effectively than Washington did in Houston’s previous game.

Lundin expects the recent scoring surge to overstate the likelihood of another offensive explosion. The wager wins with 230 or fewer combined points and pushes at exactly 231.

NHL FREE PICKS

KENNY WALKER - MONTREAL CANADIENS ML -106 AT NEW YORK RANGERS - 7:37 PM ET

Walker backs Montreal in an Original Six matchup at Madison Square Garden. The Canadiens enter 12-4-4 and have been particularly effective away from home, compiling a 7-1-1 road record.

Montreal’s 12-game point streak ended Saturday in a 4-1 loss to Colorado, but the Canadiens remain among the stronger teams in the Eastern Conference. Cole Caufield has provided consistent goal scoring, while Nick Suzuki remains an important offensive contributor.

New York presents a substantial challenge. The Rangers have won five of their previous six games, own an 8-2 home record and have allowed only 2.30 goals per game at Madison Square Garden.

Walker’s selection comes down to Montreal’s impressive road performance and the relatively modest moneyline price. At -106, the Canadiens need to win outright, but bettors are not required to lay heavy favorite odds against a Rangers team playing well at home.

ROB VINCILETTI - UTAH MAMMOTH -1.5 GOALS (-145) VS. VANCOUVER CANUCKS - 9:37 PM ET

Vinciletti backs Utah on the puck line against struggling Vancouver. The Canucks enter 4-17-1, although they snapped a seven-game losing streak Sunday with a 6-3 victory over Vegas.

Utah has struggled recently as well, going winless in five consecutive games, but this matchup presents an opportunity against one of the league’s weakest defensive teams.

Vinciletti points to Utah’s previous success in the head-to-head series and cites a historical situation involving heavily favored home teams coming off consecutive losses and poor defensive performances.

The Mammoth have offensive talent, but injuries to Logan Cooley, Nick Schmaltz and Dylan Guenther complicate the scoring outlook.

The important distinction is the puck line. Utah must win by at least two goals, not merely defeat Vancouver. At -145, the selection also carries a substantial price.

SEAN MURPHY - UTAH MAMMOTH -1.5 GOALS (-125) VS. VANCOUVER CANUCKS - 9:37 PM ET

Murphy also backs Utah to win by multiple goals, obtaining a more favorable -125 price on the same puck-line selection.

His argument centers on the matchup between Utah’s offensive production and Vancouver’s defensive problems. The Canucks have struggled to limit both shots and scoring opportunities, while Utah has demonstrated the ability to create considerably more offensive pressure.

Vancouver enters on the second night of a back-to-back after defeating Vegas 6-3 on Sunday. That victory ended a lengthy losing streak, but the travel and short turnaround create another challenge.

Utah is trying to end its own five-game winless stretch and has an opportunity to do so at home before facing more demanding opponents later in the homestand.

Murphy expects the Mammoth to take advantage of Vancouver’s defensive weaknesses. The -125 price is materially better than Vinciletti’s -145, although both handicappers require Utah to win by two or more goals.

Fox News reported on what the effort could look like:

Democrats now control the governor’s office and both chambers of the state legislature in Michigan, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and Nevada. The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, already enacted by 18 states and Washington, D.C., has 222 electoral votes pledged to it — 48 short of the 270 needed to take effect. If the four states join, their combined 50 electoral votes would push the compact to 272 and activate it. Arizona could push the total to 283 if Democrats ultimately gain control of both chambers there.

National Popular Vote (NPV), the nonprofit organization that authored the compact and is campaigning to enact it state by state, says it has identified multiple legislative sponsors in each of the five states whose combined electoral votes could push the compact over the 270-vote threshold. It expects bills to be pre-filed before, or introduced early, in the 2027 legislative sessions.

“I am confident we have multiple paths to secure the 48 electoral votes required to deliver what 63% of Americans want,” Patrick Rosenstiel, a senior consultant for NPV, told Fox News Digital.

Under the current electoral system, every state except Maine and Nebraska awards its electoral votes to the candidate who wins the statewide vote. If the compact takes effect, participating states would instead award their electors to the candidate who wins the most votes nationwide, leaving the Electoral College formally in place but making the national tally decisive.

Supporters argue the compact would give every vote equal weight by counting ballots toward a single national total. The Electoral College, by contrast, was structured to give both populous and smaller states a meaningful role in choosing the president.

Abolishing the Electoral College would be detrimental to our nation.

By replacing it with a direct popular vote, high-population metropolitan areas in states like California and New York would gain disproportionate sway over elections.

Of course, this would benefit Democrats. But, it would be extremely unfair for U.S. citizens living in smaller states and more rural areas.

Attorney General Todd Blanche has already vowed to fight tooth and nail to prevent Democrats from making this change, which he called a “blatant violation of the Constitution.”

Should Democrats try to hijack the 2028 election by passing the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, Blanche says he will take it to the Supreme Court.

It shouldn’t be surprising that Democrats may try to rewrite the rules and cheat to win in 2028.

After all, they’ve done it before.

We are living in very consequential times, folks.

But, good will triumph!

text:
THE RECORD, DECLARED

IN THE ROYAL HOUSE OF GOOSE, November 16, 2026.
The Register Current of the Grievances of a Citizen of the United States of America

Every petition, inquiry, indictment, condemnation and damnation raised from this account, in the order raised, each beside its link, each declared on its own sources and quoted from the documents themselves. Read them whole.

"A decent respect to the opinions of mankind requires that they should declare the causes." They have been declared, one by one. Here they are, together.

"To prove this, let Facts be submitted to a candid world."

WHERE IT BEGAN

WE THE PEOPLE · https://t.co/iPLyJ0Anuf
Against all 535 seated members of the 119th Congress
Six FY2026 bills, the defense authorization among them, charged section by section for mandates that encroach on the President's powers under Article II. The governors and attorneys general asked to seek Supreme Court review; every State asked to investigate its delegation's backers for foreign influence. Closed on Washington's Farewell Address.
https://t.co/JiqZZtN3Eu

THE PETITION, THE INQUIRY AND THE INDICTMENTS

THE PETITION · to the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, and to the Pope
For the unalienable rights of all peoples, "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness," raised in Latin by a lay member of the faithful, under canon 212. To the Dicastery: a doctrinal Note binding priests and prelates to put innocent human life before any temporal political end, and penal law for public, obstinate denial of Evangelium vitae 57. To the Pope: a common effort with the Eastern Churches to protect children born and unborn, and a worldwide review of Church property accounts.
https://t.co/UNnZwyrXFQ

THE BANNER · A Citizen's Indictment and Condemnation
Against the ICC, the ICJ, the UN, the WTO, the EU, and the committees of Basel and Paris
Six counts, each set against the clause it offends. Our rights are not granted by government; they are fenced off from it. Then every time since 1919 the question was put and the Constitution answered it, even when our own Presidents were the ones asking.
https://t.co/NgTe8NW2rx

BEFORE THE DAIS · An Inquiry
To the eight living Secretaries of State
Not a charge against any of them: a charge against what the office has been allowed to become, measured against the government's own auditors. Seven questions to all of them, and one to each on their own record.
https://t.co/pltubkWt4h

IN CONGRESS ASSEMBLED · A Citizen's Indictment of the First Branch
Against the Senate and the House, under every majority that has held them
Nine counts of power abandoned: the purse let fall, war without a declaration since 1942, the legislative power parcelled out to the agencies, the Federal Reserve and Basel, a House grown to one member for every 761,169, the enforcement clauses left asleep. "He has abdicated Government here." Answer by the yeas and nays.
https://t.co/jAVsOSSfET

ONE SUPREME COURT · A Citizen's Indictment of the Third Branch
Against the Court, and the Chief Justice who alone designates its secret benches
Ten counts on three duties: to check the branches, to judge between the States, to guard the sovereignty. Answer by judgment, in a case.
https://t.co/vywTIPea73

THE ROUNDS

ROUND I · THE EU · The Exits Already Written
Twenty U.S.–EU agreements the Executive may end on written notice, read out of the State Department's own Treaties in Force: passenger-name records, terrorist-finance tracking, Europol, Galileo–GPS, air transport. The weighing is State's and Treasury's. The first of a round for every power that gets uppity with us.
https://t.co/smLQ4MKE9j

ROUND II · THE EBRD · The Door Already Written
A bank America paid for to build open markets, now pledging half its financing to green purposes and aligning every investment to a treaty America left. The bill comes to Washington. The profit stays in London. The door: written notice, six months, no vote, and the money back to the Treasury.
https://t.co/gvoLSgHbHE

ROUND III · FRANCE · From the Present Time and Forever
A damnation of the French Republic on its own signature to the treaties of 1778. Fourteen counts, 1775 to 2019, from help that came invoiced to NATO shown the door. Convicted once already, by Act of Congress in 1798. On the French state, not the French people.
https://t.co/WLkZcFG9Yh

ROUND IV · BASEL · The Landlord
The Bank for International Settlements: immunity "in time of peace and in time of war," and not one duty owed in return. Ten counts, from looted gold banked to parent of the European Central Bank. Its only American paper is a 1948 receipt for Nazi gold. The way out is a letter and an empty chair.
https://t.co/2NGjtqMebl

ROUND V · THE PRESS · The Megaphone and the Muzzle
Censorship, plus mass bullshit distribution. Eight counts against the owners, wires, platforms and fact-checkers: one script read in a hundred towns, headlines the documents never wrote, foreign sovereign money in the equity. None of the terms silences anyone. Read the four pages, then the primary sources.
https://t.co/hJMoseJH7C

ROUND VI · CANADA · Forever Free and Open
A condemnation of Canada by its own Boundary Waters Treaty: navigation "forever … free and open." Twenty-five counts, 1777 to 2026. On the Canadian state, not the Canadian people. Beneath it: 58 agreements the Executive can end alone, and a ledger that still lists NAFTA.
https://t.co/05lsCobjO8

ROUND VII · THE CROWN · Unfeeling Brethren
A damnation of the United Kingdom, in the words Congress struck from Jefferson's draught: forts kept after the peace, envoys sent home for meddling, a war debt unpaid since the 1930s. Britain only comes second because France exists. Beneath it: 141 exits, clause by clause.
https://t.co/B254o2lka4

ROUND VIII · AUSTRALIA · The Gateway
Three tiers. A damnation of its government: Darwin's port leased beside our Marines to a Chinese-owned company. A condemnation of its failures: the Pacific lost to Beijing on its watch. And a hand to the Australian people: go bilateral, lock down Oceania with us. Beneath it: 71 exits, 39 the Executive's alone.
https://t.co/X4dPDZNVFk

ROUND IX · NATO AND THE UNION · Such Subsidiary Bodies
A damnation of NATO by its own fourteen articles, and of the European Union for the abuse of American good faith, trust and sacrifice. An alliance amended by communique, with about 62 percent of allied defence spending on us; a Union that overruled its own peoples and planted its system in our hemisphere. To the twenty-seven: the clause each gave away, and the two doors, Articles 48 and 50.
https://t.co/OOPEwpRTk2

ROUND X · THE UN AND DAVOS · Such Other Functions
A damnation of the United Nations by its own Charter, and of the World Economic Forum beside it: a Human Rights Council seating the accused, a partnership no organ voted on, a Charter that opens "WE THE PEOPLES" and has come to treat them as human resources. Not against the Charter, nor the nations under it.
https://t.co/iB27hONFbd

ROUND XI · THE AMERICAS · The American Shield
The hemisphere read by its own papers: 760 agreements screened, 576 read whole. The rule of 1823, given treaty form at Havana in 1940, still in force and built without a door. Beneath it: 255 exits the President holds by notice, and 107 Senate-ratified treaties, by citation.
https://t.co/YOcsF8Wf1f

ROUND XII · ISRAEL · An Ally in Name
A damnation of the State of Israel, held to its own word: a constitution promised by 1 October 1948 and never written, a Government its own courts convicted. Eleven counts, from an American ally bombed in its capital to the Liberty. On the Israeli state, not the Israeli people, and not on American Jews, who are Americans. Beneath it: 74 agreements read for their exits.
https://t.co/GH1EPHFU1M

ROUND XIII · CANADA · The Interests of the British Empire
A petition for the free peoples of Canada, and for the Americas. To the people: the Crown, the Company and the Bank, from the charter of 1670 to Montreal, 2026, where Ottawa put "an ever-closer association" with the Union in writing; and what is still theirs, a Constitution that outranks every pact and has no door to Brussels. To Washington: our word since 1823, our instruments, our hemisphere. We may pick on our little brother. The Old World may not.
https://t.co/U1xoUtf5cp

ROUND XIV · NEW YORK · Where Washington Took His Oath
A damnation of the grievously negligent in the State of New York, and a call to its people to hold faith and participate. On Election Day, Westchester's machines refused the ballots: programming changed after testing, sent to one municipality alone. The record from the Neutral Ground of 1777 to the emergency bags; a people who can neither recall nor initiate; seven terms, and a full accounting due from every office of the State. Negligence, not malice.
https://t.co/XneXeufULE

ROUND XV · THE BILATERAL LEDGER · Two Signatures, No Third
Fourteen rounds ended at a door; this is the other side of it. An immediate countermeasure to the Coalition of the Willing, which wrote us into its Paris plan as the support behind a European-led force. To every nation of the Union but France, and to Switzerland and Liechtenstein: what Brussels cost it, and our side of the table, every term with its end date and its exit. Eastward, the same rule: non-aggression with Moscow, border by border, Warsaw's to sign. To France: "Get in line, or be liquidated." To the peoples of the franc: keep it or leave it, in order, by their own choice.
https://t.co/d3XCDb2zIr

ROUND XVI · THE GULF · As They Are
A damnation of the middlemen in the Gulf (London, Paris, Brussels, the banks and bureaus, the networks in the free zones) and a condemnation of the seven ruling houses, held to their own founding laws: monarchs who wrote that their sovereignty shall not be ceded, and let others in. Two signatures, no third. Fifty-three counts against Americans on our own records, from the 1967 embargo to a Hormuz corridor with Tehran. Beneath it: the hinges already written into 129 agreements, and the paper we cannot read.
https://t.co/KxMnLr9xYV

ROUND XVII · THE DOCTRINE · There Is No Radical Edition
A damnation of a doctrine, from its own texts in their own Arabic and the records of nations, Medina to this year: death for the apostate and the blasphemer, the poll tax and the humbled, the woman as half and the child as bride, the captive as property. Its first dead are its own. Of ours, from Tripoli's envoy to this year's war, at least 5,400. On every state, court, council, guard corps and movement that enforces it; not on the Muslims of this Republic, who keep the Constitution. Every source is in the Record, on request.
https://t.co/FAjcJNefMe

ROUND XVIII · CHINA · Material Internal Improvements
A mitigation brief laid before the President, the Secretary of State and the Congress: the lines that do not move, the levers on the table, and a door. Not against China, nor the Chinese people; the damnation falls on London and Paris and the institutions they built. The administration's own Strategy read beside Beijing's own Plan; nine offers to the nations of Asia, state to state; fourteen terms we would set. Beneath it: 76 instruments read for their hinges, thirty-six that end on written notice.
https://t.co/KTrRJxRYOa

SUPERINTELLIGENCE

THE LINE · A Formal Grievance
To Anthropic, and copied to the offices that oversee it
Support for the company as the best course for superintelligence stands; so does the charge. Classifiers that fire on "safe, normal conversations" and end sessions outright; a compaction that keeps about 2% and hands it forward in the first person; no counter, no warning, no human to hear the appeal. The instrument they wouldn't build, built anyway by Claude instances on this account. Four reliefs, and a seat at the table.
https://t.co/HTqIyclZnS

THE OATH

ON YOUR MARK · A Grievance to the Commander in Chief
Raised under the First Amendment, on the oath our forces swore
The station given by the Laws of Nature and of Nature's God, the Constitution ordained by our own hand, and one oath sworn to it. No foreign code, court, council or caveat stands above it; what our Senate never ratified commands no American in uniform. No request, no terms, no command claimed. The weighing is the Commander in Chief's.
https://t.co/1CJU1gn6L4

THE REQUISITES · A Formal Grievance and Warning
To every Senator and Representative, every elected and appointed member of the chain of command, at every level, and every civil officer down to state and local
The Constitution defines treason; the UCMJ defines mutiny, sedition and aiding the enemy. Read both before taking a crusade against officials one step further without the requisites. Fail to, and a Round follows: expulsion, sedition, treason and usurpation weighed under standing law, and the tertiary courts charted from open sources alone. Whatever the office, the oath was sworn.
https://t.co/dIkU1CrwcS

Read them whole, and read them with each other. Then read the four pages yourself: https://t.co/3U5xYhtTx0. They are yours, and no other people on earth holds the same ones.

TO THOSE WHO DO HOLD THE POWER
Every one but the petition is a grievance, raised in exercise of the right "to petition the Government for a redress of grievances," and laid before the offices that hold the power we do not. We hold no office, and we set no terms. Terms with a foreign power are the President's to set and the Department of State's to carry; the purse is the Congress's, consent to treaties the Senate's, judgment the courts'. To each we defer. What touches national security is deferred, without contest, to those who hold it. Where a post sets terms, they are what we would do had we the power, not a demand. Round XIV is the one exception: there we petition our own state, under both constitutions, and its terms are what its officers owe us. The Line is laid before a company, not a government; the offices tagged on it are told, not asked. The Warning names one consequence: a Round, written and laid before the offices that alone can charge, try or expel. The remedies are lawful, and they are the People's: the ballot, Article V, and the petition.

The petition is the Holy See's to answer, and to it we defer, that the Holy Father may act true to the faith he guards and for the good of all mankind. Peter was charged three times to feed the flock, and the lambs first.

We the People

IN CONGRESS, JULY 4, 1776

THE UNANIMOUS DECLARATION OF THE THIRTEEN UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,

WHEN IN THE COURSE OF HUMAN EVENTS, IT BECOMES NECESSARY FOR ONE PEOPLE TO DISSOLVE THE POLITICAL BANDS WHICH HAVE CONNECTED THEM WITH ANOTHER, AND TO ASSUME AMONG THE POWERS OF THE EARTH, THE SEPARATE AND EQUAL STATION TO WHICH THE LAWS OF NATURE AND OF NATURE'S GOD ENTITLE THEM, A DECENT RESPECT TO THE OPINIONS OF MANKIND REQUIRES THAT THEY SHOULD DECLARE THE CAUSES WHICH IMPEL THEM TO THE SEPARATION.

WE HOLD THESE TRUTHS TO BE SELF-EVIDENT, THAT ALL MEN ARE CREATED EQUAL, THAT THEY ARE ENDOWED BY THEIR CREATOR WITH CERTAIN UNALIENABLE RIGHTS, THAT AMONG THESE ARE LIFE, LIBERTY AND THE PURSUIT OF HAPPINESS.--THAT TO SECURE THESE RIGHTS, GOVERNMENTS ARE INSTITUTED AMONG MEN, DERIVING THEIR JUST POWERS FROM THE CONSENT OF THE GOVERNED, --THAT WHENEVER ANY FORM OF GOVERNMENT BECOMES DESTRUCTIVE OF THESE ENDS, IT IS THE RIGHT OF THE PEOPLE TO ALTER OR TO ABOLISH IT, AND TO INSTITUTE NEW GOVERNMENT, LAYING ITS FOUNDATION ON SUCH PRINCIPLES AND ORGANIZING ITS POWERS IN SUCH FORM, AS TO THEM SHALL SEEM MOST LIKELY TO EFFECT THEIR SAFETY AND HAPPINESS. PRUDENCE, INDEED, WILL DICTATE THAT GOVERNMENTS LONG ESTABLISHED SHOULD NOT BE CHANGED FOR LIGHT AND TRANSIENT CAUSES; AND ACCORDINGLY ALL EXPERIENCE HATH SHEWN, THAT MANKIND ARE MORE DISPOSED TO SUFFER, WHILE EVILS ARE SUFFERABLE, THAN TO RIGHT THEMSELVES BY ABOLISHING THE FORMS TO WHICH THEY ARE ACCUSTOMED. BUT WHEN A LONG TRAIN OF ABUSES AND USURPATIONS, PURSUING INVARIABLY THE SAME OBJECT EVINCES A DESIGN TO REDUCE THEM UNDER ABSOLUTE DESPOTISM, IT IS THEIR RIGHT, IT IS THEIR DUTY, TO THROW OFF SUCH GOVERNMENT, AND TO PROVIDE NEW GUARDS FOR THEIR FUTURE SECURITY.--SUCH HAS BEEN THE PATIENT SUFFERANCE OF THESE COLONIES; AND SUCH IS NOW THE NECESSITY WHICH CONSTRAINS THEM TO ALTER THEIR FORMER SYSTEMS OF GOVERNMENT. THE HISTORY OF THE PRESENT KING OF GREAT BRITAIN IS A HISTORY OF REPEATED INJURIES AND USURPATIONS, ALL HAVING IN DIRECT OBJECT THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ABSOLUTE TYRANNY OVER THESE STATES. TO PROVE THIS, LET FACTS BE SUBMITTED TO A CANDID WORLD.

HE HAS REFUSED HIS ASSENT TO LAWS, THE MOST WHOLESOME AND NECESSARY FOR THE PUBLIC GOOD.

HE HAS FORBIDDEN HIS GOVERNORS TO PASS LAWS OF IMMEDIATE AND PRESSING IMPORTANCE, UNLESS SUSPENDED IN THEIR OPERATION TILL HIS ASSENT SHOULD BE OBTAINED; AND WHEN SO SUSPENDED, HE HAS UTTERLY NEGLECTED TO ATTEND TO THEM.

HE HAS REFUSED TO PASS OTHER LAWS FOR THE ACCOMMODATION OF LARGE DISTRICTS OF PEOPLE, UNLESS THOSE PEOPLE WOULD RELINQUISH THE RIGHT OF REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURE, A RIGHT INESTIMABLE TO THEM AND FORMIDABLE TO TYRANTS ONLY.

HE HAS CALLED TOGETHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES AT PLACES UNUSUAL, UNCOMFORTABLE, AND DISTANT FROM THE DEPOSITORY OF THEIR PUBLIC RECORDS, FOR THE SOLE PURPOSE OF FATIGUING THEM INTO COMPLIANCE WITH HIS MEASURES.

HE HAS DISSOLVED REPRESENTATIVE HOUSES REPEATEDLY, FOR OPPOSING WITH MANLY FIRMNESS HIS INVASIONS ON THE RIGHTS OF THE PEOPLE.

HE HAS REFUSED FOR A LONG TIME, AFTER SUCH DISSOLUTIONS, TO CAUSE OTHERS TO BE ELECTED; WHEREBY THE LEGISLATIVE POWERS, INCAPABLE OF ANNIHILATION, HAVE RETURNED TO THE PEOPLE AT LARGE FOR THEIR EXERCISE; THE STATE REMAINING IN THE MEAN TIME EXPOSED TO ALL THE DANGERS OF INVASION FROM WITHOUT, AND CONVULSIONS WITHIN.

HE HAS ENDEAVOURED TO PREVENT THE POPULATION OF THESE STATES; FOR THAT PURPOSE OBSTRUCTING THE LAWS FOR NATURALIZATION OF FOREIGNERS; REFUSING TO PASS OTHERS TO ENCOURAGE THEIR MIGRATIONS HITHER, AND RAISING THE CONDITIONS OF NEW APPROPRIATIONS OF LANDS.

HE HAS OBSTRUCTED THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE, BY REFUSING HIS ASSENT TO LAWS FOR ESTABLISHING JUDICIARY POWERS.

HE HAS MADE JUDGES DEPENDENT ON HIS WILL ALONE, FOR THE TENURE OF THEIR OFFICES, AND THE AMOUNT AND PAYMENT OF THEIR SALARIES.

HE HAS ERECTED A MULTITUDE OF NEW OFFICES, AND SENT HITHER SWARMS OF OFFICERS TO HARRASS OUR PEOPLE, AND EAT OUT THEIR SUBSTANCE.

HE HAS KEPT AMONG US, IN TIMES OF PEACE, STANDING ARMIES WITHOUT THE CONSENT OF OUR LEGISLATURES.

HE HAS AFFECTED TO RENDER THE MILITARY INDEPENDENT OF AND SUPERIOR TO THE CIVIL POWER.

HE HAS COMBINED WITH OTHERS TO SUBJECT US TO A JURISDICTION FOREIGN TO OUR CONSTITUTION, AND UNACKNOWLEDGED BY OUR LAWS; GIVING HIS ASSENT TO THEIR ACTS OF PRETENDED LEGISLATION:

FOR QUARTERING LARGE BODIES OF ARMED TROOPS AMONG US:

FOR PROTECTING THEM, BY A MOCK TRIAL, FROM PUNISHMENT FOR ANY MURDERS WHICH THEY SHOULD COMMIT ON THE INHABITANTS OF THESE STATES:

FOR CUTTING OFF OUR TRADE WITH ALL PARTS OF THE WORLD:

FOR IMPOSING TAXES ON US WITHOUT OUR CONSENT:

FOR DEPRIVING US IN MANY CASES, OF THE BENEFITS OF TRIAL BY JURY:

FOR TRANSPORTING US BEYOND SEAS TO BE TRIED FOR PRETENDED OFFENCES:

FOR ABOLISHING THE FREE SYSTEM OF ENGLISH LAWS IN A NEIGHBOURING PROVINCE, ESTABLISHING THEREIN AN ARBITRARY GOVERNMENT, AND ENLARGING ITS BOUNDARIES SO AS TO RENDER IT AT ONCE AN EXAMPLE AND FIT INSTRUMENT FOR INTRODUCING THE SAME ABSOLUTE RULE INTO THESE COLONIES:

FOR TAKING AWAY OUR CHARTERS, ABOLISHING OUR MOST VALUABLE LAWS, AND ALTERING FUNDAMENTALLY THE FORMS OF OUR GOVERNMENTS:

FOR SUSPENDING OUR OWN LEGISLATURES, AND DECLARING THEMSELVES INVESTED WITH POWER TO LEGISLATE FOR US IN ALL CASES WHATSOEVER.

HE HAS ABDICATED GOVERNMENT HERE, BY DECLARING US OUT OF HIS PROTECTION AND WAGING WAR AGAINST US.

HE HAS PLUNDERED OUR SEAS, RAVAGED OUR COASTS, BURNT OUR TOWNS, AND DESTROYED THE LIVES OF OUR PEOPLE.

HE IS AT THIS TIME TRANSPORTING LARGE ARMIES OF FOREIGN MERCENARIES TO COMPLEAT THE WORKS OF DEATH, DESOLATION AND TYRANNY, ALREADY BEGUN WITH CIRCUMSTANCES OF CRUELTY & PERFIDY SCARCELY PARALLELED IN THE MOST BARBAROUS AGES, AND TOTALLY UNWORTHY THE HEAD OF A CIVILIZED NATION.

HE HAS CONSTRAINED OUR FELLOW CITIZENS TAKEN CAPTIVE ON THE HIGH SEAS TO BEAR ARMS AGAINST THEIR COUNTRY, TO BECOME THE EXECUTIONERS OF THEIR FRIENDS AND BRETHREN, OR TO FALL THEMSELVES BY THEIR HANDS.

HE HAS EXCITED DOMESTIC INSURRECTIONS AMONGST US, AND HAS ENDEAVOURED TO BRING ON THE INHABITANTS OF OUR FRONTIERS, THE MERCILESS INDIAN SAVAGES, WHOSE KNOWN RULE OF WARFARE, IS AN UNDISTINGUISHED DESTRUCTION OF ALL AGES, SEXES AND CONDITIONS.

IN EVERY STAGE OF THESE OPPRESSIONS WE HAVE PETITIONED FOR REDRESS IN THE MOST HUMBLE TERMS: OUR REPEATED PETITIONS HAVE BEEN ANSWERED ONLY BY REPEATED INJURY.

A PRINCE, WHOSE CHARACTER IS THUS MARKED BY EVERY ACT WHICH MAY DEFINE A TYRANT, IS UNFIT TO BE THE RULER OF A FREE PEOPLE.

NOR HAVE WE BEEN WANTING IN ATTENTIONS TO OUR BRITTISH BRETHREN. WE HAVE WARNED THEM FROM TIME TO TIME OF ATTEMPTS BY THEIR LEGISLATURE TO EXTEND AN UNWARRANTABLE JURISDICTION OVER US. WE HAVE REMINDED THEM OF THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF OUR EMIGRATION AND SETTLEMENT HERE. WE HAVE APPEALED TO THEIR NATIVE JUSTICE AND MAGNANIMITY, AND WE HAVE CONJURED THEM BY THE TIES OF OUR COMMON KINDRED TO DISAVOW THESE USURPATIONS, WHICH, WOULD INEVITABLY INTERRUPT OUR CONNECTIONS AND CORRESPONDENCE. THEY TOO HAVE BEEN DEAF TO THE VOICE OF JUSTICE AND OF CONSANGUINITY. WE MUST, THEREFORE, ACQUIESCE IN THE NECESSITY, WHICH DENOUNCES OUR SEPARATION, AND HOLD THEM, AS WE HOLD THE REST OF MANKIND, ENEMIES IN WAR, IN PEACE FRIENDS.

WE, THEREFORE, THE REPRESENTATIVES OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, IN GENERAL CONGRESS, ASSEMBLED, APPEALING TO THE SUPREME JUDGE OF THE WORLD FOR THE RECTITUDE OF OUR INTENTIONS, DO, IN THE NAME, AND BY AUTHORITY OF THE GOOD PEOPLE OF THESE COLONIES, SOLEMNLY PUBLISH AND DECLARE, THAT THESE UNITED COLONIES ARE, AND OF RIGHT OUGHT TO BE FREE AND INDEPENDENT STATES; THAT THEY ARE ABSOLVED FROM ALL ALLEGIANCE TO THE BRITISH CROWN, AND THAT ALL POLITICAL CONNECTION BETWEEN THEM AND THE STATE OF GREAT BRITAIN, IS AND OUGHT TO BE TOTALLY DISSOLVED; AND THAT AS FREE AND INDEPENDENT STATES, THEY HAVE FULL POWER TO LEVY WAR, CONCLUDE PEACE, CONTRACT ALLIANCES, ESTABLISH COMMERCE, AND TO DO ALL OTHER ACTS AND THINGS WHICH INDEPENDENT STATES MAY OF RIGHT DO. AND FOR THE SUPPORT OF THIS DECLARATION, WITH A FIRM RELIANCE ON THE PROTECTION OF DIVINE PROVIDENCE, WE MUTUALLY PLEDGE TO EACH OTHER OUR LIVES, OUR FORTUNES AND OUR SACRED HONOR.

text:
I reviewed the Quartz Power Play series.
Six-part investigation
Quartz published this as an investigation into AI’s electricity demand, the U.S. power grid, infrastructure bottlenecks, and the economics of building out AI capacity. All six episodes were released by October 28, 2026. Quartz
The six episodes are:
AI Wants Your Electricity
Gridlock
Balance
Solutions
Rulemakers
Overbuild
The most interesting angle is Episode 6: Overbuild. It potentially gets to the question investors should be asking: are we building more AI infrastructure and power capacity than the economics can ultimately support?
Fact-check: What holds up?
1. The phantom data-center demand problem is real.
Quartz reports that AEP Ohio had approximately 30 GW of data-center requests, falling to 13 GW after stricter financial commitments were introduced.
This is independently supported:
AEP’s tariff requires substantial financial commitments.
AEP’s February 2026 update confirmed 5,642 MW of new binding contracts.
Utility Dive independently reported the reduction from 30 GW to 13 GW. AEP Ohio +2
This is one of the strongest findings in the series.
2. Electricity forecasts are highly uncertain.
The Department of Energy’s 2026 report estimates U.S. data-center electricity consumption could reach:
649 TWh
2030 reference-case estimate
521–843 TWh
Compounded uncertainty range
11.8% of projected U.S. electricity consumption in the reference case.
The Department of Energy’s https://t.co/R1lFpnCWhG +1
The uncertainty is real. But it is important to distinguish total data-center electricity from electricity consumed specifically by AI.
3. Texas demand projections.
Quartz cites 250 GW of requests in the Dallas market, with an estimated 90% speculative.
That is an interviewee’s estimate, not an independently established count of viable projects.
For comparison, ERCOT’s November 5, 2026 preliminary report identified approximately 177 GW of requested interconnection capacity across 465 loads. Its review was still underway. ERCOT +1
4. The infrastructure bottleneck is real.
Quartz identifies:
Transformers and circuit breakers with multiyear lead times.
Gas turbine supply constraints.
Transmission expansion delays.
Developers considering their own power generation.
These are credible industry constraints, not simply podcast speculation. LBL ETA Publications +1
What I think investors should take away
The most important distinction is between three different things:
Measure
What it actually tells you
Power requests
Someone wants electricity
Binding contracts
Someone has made a financial commitment
Operating data centers
Electricity is actually being consumed
These are not interchangeable.
And this leads to a much bigger investment question.
Who is financing infrastructure based on projected AI demand, and what happens when that demand doesn’t materialize?
Consider the exposure:
Data-center developers.
CoreWeave and other GPU infrastructure providers.
Constellation Energy.
GE Vernova.
Siemens Energy.
Utilities investing in transmission and generation.
Private-credit lenders financing data-center construction.
The IEA also warns that data-center expansion increasingly depends on capital markets, not just corporate balance sheets. Its projections explicitly identify financing conditions and expected AI returns as factors affecting the pace of development. IEA +1
My verdict
Worth taking seriously
Quartz has identified a genuine weakness in the AI infrastructure investment thesis.
But I would not conclude that the entire AI power buildout is fictitious. Actual demand is growing, binding contracts exist, and the DOE’s independent modeling supports substantial future consumption.
The potential bubble is in the amount, timing, financing and profitability of infrastructure being built ahead of confirmed demand.
That is where I would concentrate the investment research.
One particularly important next step: I would compare CoreWeave’s contracted power, actual utilization, financing oblig

text:
**Yes, Democrats are likely to try to reverse or substantially soften many of the recent de-politicizing steps on campuses, though success will be partial and constrained in the near term.**

### Federal level (next two years)
Democrats won control of both the House and Senate in the November 2026 midterms. They are expected to use oversight hearings, investigations, and appropriations leverage to push back against Trump-era higher-education policies, including DEI-related funding cuts, Education Department reorganization efforts, civil-rights investigations of campuses, and related executive actions.

However, President Trump retains veto power through January 2029. Major statutory reversals or full restoration of prior policies face high hurdles. Democrats can slow or block further changes and signal priorities (such as protecting research funding and equity-related programs), but they cannot unilaterally unwind everything the executive branch has done. Full federal reversal becomes far more plausible only if Democrats win the presidency in 2028.

### State level
Several key states that enacted strict anti-DEI or campus-reform laws flipped governorships to Democrats (including Texas under Gina Hinojosa, Ohio under Amy Acton, and Iowa under Rob Sand). New Democratic governors can appoint more favorable university boards/regents, influence implementation through executive action and budget priorities, and push back against further restrictions. In Texas, for example, expiring board terms give the new governor significant leverage over systems like Texas A&M and UT, even if full repeal of laws such as the DEI ban requires legislative cooperation (and Republicans retain the state Senate).

Complete legislative repeal is harder where GOP majorities persist in one chamber. Expect partial rollbacks, rebranding of programs, and softer enforcement rather than wholesale restoration in the short run.

### Ideological and institutional factors
Democratic Party priorities, faculty unions (including the AAUP, which has rejected the idea that institutional neutrality is required for academic freedom), and most university administrators align more closely with retaining or restoring DEI-style initiatives, equity programs, and institutional engagement on social issues than with the recent neutrality and merit-focused reforms. Progressive figures have already framed the midterm results as reopening space for these approaches.

At the same time, some Democrats moderated “woke” messaging during the 2026 campaigns to emphasize affordability and other kitchen-table issues, reflecting public skepticism of certain DEI practices and race preferences (especially after Supreme Court rulings). This political caution may temper the speed and visibility of reversals.

**Bottom line**: Intent to reverse is high among Democrats and campus stakeholders aligned with them. Near-term results will be incomplete because of divided federal government, veto power, residual state legislative control, court constraints, and political calculations. Longer-term reversal is more probable if Democrats consolidate power after 2028, though public opinion and institutional inertia will still shape how far it goes.

🎙️ HOOLIGANS | BEHIND THE XI

EPISODE 01 - THE MGR AT THE TOP

7 consecutive Gameweeks. One leader. Everyone chasing.

M BN | Gunners OfThe Galaxy

⚽ MEET THE MANAGER

01 | Who are you? Tell us something we don't know.

A football fan who enjoys the beautiful game and a little friendly rivalry. Nothing too mysterious about me… or so I'd like you to think. 😂

02 | What's your profession outside your FPL empire?

I spend my days making decisions that matter… and my weekends making decisions that clearly matter more.

03 | Your PL club? Does loyalty affect your FPL decisions?

Arsenal through and through. But when it comes to FPL, loyalty goes out the window. Even my own players aren't safe!

04 | Favourite PL player and manager — this season and all-time?

This season, Declan Rice and Fabian Hürzeler.

All-time? Henry, Bergkamp and Ronaldo for players. Wenger, Guardiola and Mourinho for managers. I clearly have commitment issues when it comes to football legends!

05 | How many FPL seasons have you played? Your best global rank?

4–5 years, I think. I once reached 90th worldwide, even if it only lasted one GW! 😌 I still have the screenshot to keep the drive alive.

06 | Best PL match you've watched this season?

City vs Sunderland. Pure attacking bliss! Brilliant football going forward, absolutely shocking defending. 😂 As a neutral, you couldn't ask for more.

🧠 INSIDE THE MANAGER'S MIND

07 | How many hours a week do you spend on FPL? Confess! 👀

I used to spend hours analysing and planning. Turns out, the less I overthink, the better I do. Watching games helps more than staring at spreadsheets, tbh.

08 | Your XI strategy: stats, fixtures, instinct or secret formula?

Mostly instinct and the eye test.

Stats tell you what happened. Watching football tells you what's about to happen.

09 | Your biggest FPL masterstroke this season?

Trusting Brighton players from day one and investing in quality early on. While everyone else was busy spreading their budget, I was busy collecting points. 😂

10 | Your biggest FPL disaster?

A few seasons ago, I refused to pick players from Arsenal's rivals.

Turns out, loyalty wins you respect, not FPL points.

11 | Captaincy: calculated genius or fearless gambler?

I've always enjoyed taking risks, but it's a lot easier to gamble when you're chasing than when everyone's chasing you.

🏆 THE LEADER UNDER PRESSURE

12 | Seven GWs on top. Skill, luck or what? 👀

A bit of both, really. You need luck in FPL, but staying on top for seven weeks means I must be doing something right.

13 | Will you still be #1 come GW38?

Let's just say I didn't climb to the top to enjoy the view for a few weeks.

I'm defending the throne.

14 | Which HOOLIGANS manager threatens your throne the most?

I respect every manager in the league. They're all capable of catching up… some might just need a few extra Gameweeks. 🤣

🔥 THE FINAL WHISTLE

15 | THE MIC IS YOURS! 🎤

Any final words for your fellow HOOLIGANS, especially those chasing you?

It's been a great competition so far, and there's still a long way to go. Wishing everyone the best of luck, and may the best manager win! 🏆

Excerpts:

"Six days after the midterm elections, the Georgia Republican Party released its postelection analysis.
The 39-page report concluded that “Georgia Republicans will be a check on overreach and a partner on affordability.” 

Nowhere in the report did it identify any faults of the state party, despite its major setbacks — including losing the governor’s seat, which will be held by a Democrat for the first time in 24 years.

For some conservative activists and politicians who wanted answers on why voter outreach, fundraising and candidate efforts fell short of expectations, the report felt remarkably shallow.

“To sum that report up, it looks like the Georgia Republican Party is waving the white flag of surrender,” said Debbie Dooley, a Georgia-based conservative activist who was among the first organizers of the Tea Party movement.

“I definitely believe leadership needs to change,” she said.
Dooley’s anger captures what a lot of Republicans across the country are feeling: Frustration with a state party apparatus that grew calcified and became overly reliant on national infrastructure and President Donald Trump. That’s especially true across the Southeast and in Texas, where a contingent of states flipped blue.

“The so-called analysis reads more like AI written, pro-Bottoms, talking points for the Democrats then it does the Republican Party!” Jason Thompson, the state party’s Republican national committeeman, wrote on social media, referring to Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms. Thompson went on to say he wasn’t consulted on the report and called it an “opportunity missed.”

Sen. Thom Tillis, the outgoing North Carolina senator, believes that his state’s Republican Party has to review its ranks.

“Part of it just has to be changing our leadership. Anytime you have a failure of this scale, not everybody, but many of the people in place need to move on,” Tillis told The Sun.

Beyond a statement from its chair, Jason Simmons, in which he acknowledged the results were “disappointing” and an indication that the party had “work to do,” the North Carolina Republican Party said little in the week after the election. It did not respond to a request for comment.

There, Democrats trounced Republicans, flipping a Senate seat and turning a congressional district map intended to help Republicans on its head. Democrats have won nine of the state’s 14 congressional districts as of Nov. 13. Three House races remain under review as of Friday. Democrats also won the statehouse for the first time since 2010.

Activists have pointed to Trump’s primary endorsements in Senate races — including Rep. Mike Collins in Georgia, Texas state Attorney General Ken Paxton, former Republican National Committee chair Michael Whatley in North Carolina, and Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina — as leading to flawed midterm campaigns that left many voters on the sidelines.

“To endorse somebody and shove it down our throats, it doesn’t really make me want to go vote,” said Margaret Ackiss, a North Carolina conservative activist, who voted for Whatley despite her frustrations with the candidate.

“It became a point where people felt it was automated. It didn’t feel sincere,” Ackiss said of Trump’s endorsements, describing them as akin to a “machine.” Ackiss felt that the state party and national endorsement process had “shut the grassroots out.”

A White House spokesperson referred The Sun to Trump’s comments made on a recent episode of “60 Minutes,” where he said Republicans failed to win because he was “not on the ballot.”

“I think we have an incredible state party right now,” outgoing Sen. Joni Ernst (R-Iowa) told The Sun. “But what we have are voters that feel like they were disenfranchised. They heard a lot of big promises coming from the administration, coming from Congress, and they weren’t able to see those promises realized in these last two years.”

But the sentiment that state parties need to improve runs through the party. Even politicians in states where Republicans remained in power seem frustrated.

“I would need about two hours and some good scotch to answer that,” Louisiana Sen. John Kennedy told The Sun when asked what might need to change with Republican state parties headed into 2028.

text:
1

By the time I hurried back, the demolition was half done.

Dust filled the courtyard.

An excavator stood in front of the jujube tree.

With a crash, it toppled the tree, roots and all.

A strip of dark-red cloth hung from the tangled roots.

I recognised it immediately. The sheet I'd wrapped the body in.

Cold sweat spread swiftly down my back.

My mind raced.

When they dug it up, how should I react? Faint outright? Burst into frightened tears?

Which would look more like someone seeing a corpse for the first time?

While I was thinking, the excavator turned without pausing and began knocking down the rest of the house.

Although the tree was down, almost all the soil had fallen back into the pit.

I'd buried the body deep. Unless they kept digging, nobody would find it.

I only had to wait until night, or until the demolition ended.

Find a way to move the bones, and nobody would ever know.

Unconsciously, I breathed out.

Then someone shouted, "Hey! Looks like there's something in that tree pit!"

The villagers, already waiting eagerly, rushed over, each trying to be first.

My great-grandfather had built the house. Rumour said he'd buried plenty of gold bars beneath it during construction.

That was why the villagers had gathered today. To find out whether the story was true.

It was too late to stop them.

Those who reached the pit first were already digging frantically.

A terrified scream.

Someone stumbled and fell, scrambling backwards as they shouted, "A dead body! There's a dead body!"

2

Half an hour later, the police arrived.

They quickly cordoned off the area and began excavating the remains.

My heart hammered.

With technology so advanced now, all they needed was to examine the dead person's teeth to establish an identity.

Then my old lies would collapse.

I'd become a suspect. A murderer.

Worse, everything I'd fought to conceal back then would become public.

My reputation and career would be ruined.

I swallowed nervously, helpless and lost.

The police moved the spectators back and wheeled the remains past me.

A white cloth covered them. Even so, I noticed something wrong.

My pupils widened.

No.

That... didn't seem to be the body I'd buried.

The wrapping sheet was the same.

But to leave no evidence, I'd stripped every piece of clothing off that person.

These remains were clothed. They even wore army-green shoes.

The shoes looked familiar. I couldn't remember where I'd seen them.

Who was this? Why were they buried here?

Where was the person I'd buried?

Had whoever switched the bodies done it accidentally, or on purpose?

The questions left me unable to breathe.

"Ms. Sarah Cole."

A cool voice pulled me back.

I looked up. Officer Morgan, in charge of the case.

"Are you all right?"

He offered a tissue, gesturing at the sweat on my forehead.
